title.zh: 卷一百八十四 志第一百三十七 食貨下六
title.raw: 卷一百八十四 志第一百三十七 食貨下六 Volume 184 Treatises 137: Finance and Economics 2f

sentences.zh: 食貨下六○茶下

translations.literal: Finance and Economics, Part 6 — Tea, continued
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part 6 — Tea (continued)

sentences.zh: 茶天聖三年八月，詔翰林侍講學士孫奭等同究利害，奭等言：“十三場茶積而未售者六百一十三萬餘斤，蓋許商人貼射，則善者皆入商人，其入官者皆粗惡不時，故人莫肯售。

translations.literal: Tea. In the eighth month of the third year of Tiansheng, an edict ordered Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting Sun Shi and others jointly to investigate advantages and disadvantages. Shi and others said: "At the thirteen tea markets, unsold tea accumulated to more than 6,130,000 jin. This was because when merchants were permitted supplementary bidding, the good [tea] all went to merchants, while what entered official [stores] was all coarse, inferior, and untimely, so people were unwilling to buy."
translations.idiomatic: On tea: in the eighth month of Tiansheng 3 (1025), the court ordered Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting Sun Shi and others to study the policy’s costs and benefits together. Shi and his colleagues reported: “At the thirteen tea markets, more than 6.13 million jin of tea had piled up unsold. The reason was that once merchants were allowed supplementary bidding, all the good tea went to them, while what the government received was coarse, poor-quality, and out of season—so no one would buy it.”

sentences.zh: 又園戶輸歲課不足者，使如商人入息，而園戶皆細民，貧弱力不能給，煩擾益甚。

translations.literal: Furthermore, for plantation households who fell short of the annual levy, they were made to pay interest like merchants; but plantation households were all petty commoners, poor and weak, unable to pay, and harassment increased ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Plantation households who fell short of their annual quota were also required to pay interest like merchants—but they were petty cultivators, too poor and weak to meet the payments, and official harassment only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 又奸人倚貼射為名，強市盜販，侵奪官利，其弊不可不革。

translations.literal: Furthermore, scoundrels relied on supplementary bidding as a pretext to force sales and smuggle, encroaching on and seizing official profits; these abuses could not go unreformed.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, unscrupulous men used supplementary bidding as cover to force purchases and smuggle tea, stripping the state of its profits—abuses that had to be ended.

sentences.zh: ”十月，遂罷貼射法，官復給本錢市茶。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month, the supplementary bidding law was then abolished, and the government again provided capital funds to purchase tea.
translations.idiomatic: ” In the tenth month the supplementary-bidding system was abolished, and the government resumed advancing capital to buy tea directly.

sentences.zh: 商人入錢以售茶者，奭等又欲優之，請凡入錢京師售海州、荊南茶者，損為七萬七千，售真州等四務十三場茶者，又第損之，給茶皆直十萬。

translations.literal: For merchants who paid in money to sell tea, Shi and others also wished to favor them, requesting that for all who paid money at the capital to sell tea from Haizhou and Jingnan, [the payment] be reduced to seventy-seven thousand; for those selling tea from the four offices and thirteen markets such as Zhenzhou, it be further reduced in steps, while tea issued was all valued at one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and his colleagues also wanted to favor merchants who paid cash for tea rights: they proposed cutting the fee to 77,000 cash for those buying Haizhou and Jingnan tea at the capital, and reducing it further in tiers for tea from the four monopoly offices and thirteen markets such as Zhenzhou—while still issuing tea worth 100,000 cash in every case.

sentences.zh: 自是，河北入中復用三說法，舊給東南緡錢者，以京師榷貨務錢償之。

translations.literal: From this time, for Hebei tribute deliveries the three-item method was again used; where Southeast string-cash had formerly been given, it was repaid with money from the capital Monopoly Goods Office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hebei grain-forage deliveries again used the three-item exchange method, and former payments in Southeast string-cash were settled from the capital Monopoly Goods Office instead.

sentences.zh: 奭等議既用，益以李諮等變法為非。

translations.literal: Once Shi's proposals were adopted, he increasingly regarded Li Zi's and others' policy changes as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi’s recommendations took effect, he increasingly condemned the reforms of Li Zi and his allies as mistaken.

sentences.zh: 明年，摭計置司所上天聖二年比視增虧數差謬，詔令嚐典議官張士遜等條析。

translations.literal: The next year, it was seized upon that the Planning Office's submitted comparison of gains and losses for Tiansheng year 2 was erroneous; an edict ordered Remonstrance and Discussion Official Zhang Shixun and others to analyze it item by item.
translations.idiomatic: The following year officials seized on errors in the Planning Office’s year-on-year profit-and-loss figures for Tiansheng 2; the emperor ordered Remonstrance Official Zhang Shixun and others to parse the accounts line by line.

sentences.zh: 夷簡言：“天聖初，環慶等路數奏芻糧不給，京師府藏常闕緡錢，吏兵月奉僅能取足。

translations.literal: Yijian said: "At the beginning of Tiansheng, the circuits of Huan and Qing repeatedly memorialized that forage and grain were insufficient; the capital treasury often lacked string-cash; clerks' and soldiers' monthly salaries could barely be fully paid.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian argued: “Early in the Tiansheng reign, Huanqing and neighboring circuits repeatedly reported shortages of forage and grain; the capital treasury was chronically short of cash; and clerks’ and soldiers’ monthly pay could barely be met.

sentences.zh: 自變法以來，京師積錢多，邊計不聞告乏，中間蕃部作亂，調發兵馬，仰給有司，無不足之患。

translations.literal: Since the policy change, the capital accumulated much money; border accounts were not heard to report shortages; in the interim when frontier tribes rebelled and troops were mobilized, relying on supply from the relevant offices, there was no worry of insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reforms, cash had piled up in the capital and the frontiers no longer reported shortfalls; even when border tribes rebelled and armies were mobilized, supply offices could meet demand without strain.”

sentences.zh: 以此推之，頗有成效。

translations.literal: Judging by this, [the reforms] had considerable effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure the changes had clearly worked.

sentences.zh: 三司比視數目差互不同，非執政所能親自較計。

translations.literal: The Three Departments' comparative figures differed from one another; this was not something the chief ministers could personally verify.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments’ comparative figures simply did not agree—something no chief minister could audit by himself.”

sentences.zh: ”然士遜等猶被罰，諮罷三司使。

translations.literal: " Yet Shixun and others were still punished, and Zi was removed as Three Departments commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: ” Nevertheless Shixun and his colleagues were still penalized, and Zi was dismissed as Three Departments commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，園戶負歲課者如商人入息，後不能償。

translations.literal: At first, plantation households in arrears on the annual levy paid interest like merchants, but later could not repay.
translations.idiomatic: At first plantation households behind on their annual quotas had been charged merchant-style interest, but they soon could not pay it back.

sentences.zh: 至四年，太湖等九場凡逋息錢十三萬緡，詔悉蠲之。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, at nine markets including Taihu, arrears in interest money totaled one hundred thirty thousand strings; an edict remitted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: By year four the nine markets including Taihu owed 130,000 strings in interest; an edict remitted the entire sum.

sentences.zh: 然自奭等改製，而茶法浸壞。

translations.literal: Yet from the time Shi and others changed the system, the tea law gradually deteriorated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the moment Shi and his allies reworked the rules, the tea monopoly steadily unraveled.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，三司使孫居中等言：“自天聖三年變法，而河北入中虛估之敝，復類乾興以前，蠹耗縣官，請復行見錢法。

translations.literal: During Jingyou, Three Departments Commissioner Sun Juzhong and others said: "Since the Tiansheng year 3 policy change, the abuse of inflated valuations in Hebei tribute deliveries has again resembled the period before Qianxing, draining the state treasury; we request that the cash method be restored."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era (1034–1038), Three Departments Commissioner Sun Juzhong and others argued: “Since the Tiansheng 3 reforms, Hebei deliveries have again suffered inflated valuations like those before Qianxing, bleeding the treasury—we ask that the cash-payment method be restored.”

sentences.zh: ”時諮已執政矣。

translations.literal: " By then Zi was already in the chief ministry.
translations.idiomatic: ” By then Li Zi himself sat among the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 三年，河北轉運使楊偕亦陳三說法十二害，見錢法十二利，以謂止用三說所支一分緡錢，足以贍一歲邊計。

translations.literal: In the third year, Hebei Transport Commissioner Yang Jie also set forth twelve harms of the three-item method and twelve benefits of the cash method, stating that using only one-tenth of the string-cash paid out under the three-item method would suffice to supply a year's border accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Hebei transport commissioner Yang Jie listed twelve evils of the three-item method and twelve benefits of cash payment, claiming that a mere tenth of the string-cash spent under the three-item system would cover a full year’s frontier budget.

sentences.zh: 遂命諮與參知政事蔡齊等合議，且令詔商人訪其利害。

translations.literal: The court then ordered Zi to deliberate jointly with Vice Grand Councilor Cai Qi and others, and also commanded that merchants be summoned to report on advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zi to confer with Vice Grand Councilor Cai Qi and others, and publicly invited merchants to testify on what helped or hurt them.

sentences.zh: 是歲三月，諮等請罷河北入中虛估，以實錢償芻粟，實錢售茶，皆如天聖元年之製。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year, Zi and others requested abolishing inflated Hebei tribute valuations, repaying forage and grain with real money, and selling tea for real money—all as under the Tiansheng year 1 regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That March Zi’s group asked to end inflated Hebei valuations, pay for forage and grain in real cash, and sell tea for real cash—restoring the Tiansheng 1 rules.

sentences.zh: 又以北商持券至京師，舊必得交引鋪為之保任，並得三司符驗，然後給錢，以是京師坐賈率多邀求，三司吏稽留為奸，乃悉罷之，命商持券徑趣榷貨務驗實，立償之錢。

translations.literal: Furthermore, when northern merchants brought certificates to the capital, formerly they had to obtain guarantee from exchange-note shops and also receive Three Departments verification before money was issued; because of this, capital sedentary merchants mostly made many demands, and Three Departments clerks delayed for fraud—so all of this was abolished, ordering merchants to take certificates directly to the Monopoly Goods Office for verification and immediate payment.
translations.idiomatic: Northern merchants bringing certificates to the capital had once needed exchange-note shops to guarantee them and Three Departments seals before payment—giving local wholesalers and clerks endless chances to extort and stall. Those steps were abolished: merchants now went straight to the Monopoly Goods Office for verification and prompt cash.

sentences.zh: 初，奭等雖增商人入錢之數，而猶以為利薄，故競市虛估之券，以射厚利，而入錢者寡，縣官日以侵削，京師少蓄藏。

translations.literal: At first, although Shi and others had increased the amount merchants paid in money, [merchants] still regarded the profit as thin; therefore they competed to buy inflated certificates to seek thick profit, while those paying in money were few; the state treasury was daily eroded, and the capital had little stored wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shi’s reforms had raised merchants’ cash payments, profits still looked thin, so traders snapped up inflated certificates for outsized gains while few paid cash at all—the treasury eroded daily and capital reserves dwindled.

sentences.zh: 至是，諮等請視天聖三年入錢數第損一千有奇，入中增直亦視天聖元年數第加三百。

translations.literal: At this point, Zi and others requested that compared with Tiansheng year 3 cash payments, [fees] be reduced stepwise by somewhat more than one thousand; for tribute deliveries, valuations be increased stepwise by three hundred compared with Tiansheng year 1 figures.
translations.idiomatic: Zi’s group now proposed tiered cuts of just over 1,000 cash from the Tiansheng 3 payment schedule, and tiered increases of 300 cash on Hebei delivery valuations relative to Tiansheng 1.

sentences.zh: 詔皆可之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every item.

sentences.zh: 前已用虛估給券者，給茶如舊，仍給景祐二年已前茶。

translations.literal: For those previously issued certificates on inflated valuations, tea was issued as before, still giving tea from before Jingyou year 2.
translations.idiomatic: Certificates already issued on inflated terms still received tea as before, including stock from before Jingyou 2 (1035).

sentences.zh: 既而諮等又言：“天聖四年，嚐許陝西入中願得茶者，每錢十萬，所在給券，徑趣東南受茶十一萬一千。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Zi and others also said: "In Tiansheng year 4, it was once permitted that for Shaanxi tribute deliveries wishing to receive tea, for every one hundred thousand in money, certificates were issued locally, going directly to the Southeast to receive one hundred eleven thousand [worth of] tea.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zi’s group added: “In Tiansheng 4 the court had allowed Shaanxi deliverers who wanted tea to receive, for every 100,000 cash paid locally, certificates redeemable in the Southeast for 111,000 cash worth of tea.

sentences.zh: 茶商獲利，爭欲售陝西券，故不復入錢京師，請禁止之。

translations.literal: Tea merchants profited and competed to sell Shaanxi certificates; therefore they no longer paid money at the capital; [they] requested prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Tea merchants profited and rushed to sell Shaanxi certificates instead of paying cash in the capital—we ask that this be banned.”

sentences.zh: ”並言商人所不便者，其事甚悉，請為更約束，重私販之禁，聽商人輸錢五分，餘為置籍召保，期半年悉償，失期者倍其數。

translations.literal: " They also set forth in detail what was inconvenient for merchants, requesting revised regulations, heavier prohibition of private trafficking, permitting merchants to pay five-tenths in money, registering the remainder with summoned guarantors, requiring full repayment within half a year, with double the amount for those missing the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: ” They also catalogued every merchant grievance and proposed tighter rules, stricter bans on private trade, payment of half the fee upfront with the balance registered under guarantors due in six months—doubled if overdue.

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: All matters were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Every measure was adopted.

sentences.zh: 諮等復言：“自奭等變法，歲損財利不可勝計，且以天聖九年至景祐二年較之，五年之間，河北入中虛費緡錢五百六十八萬；

translations.literal: Zi and others again said: "Since Shi and others changed the law, annual losses in revenue cannot be fully calculated; moreover, comparing from Tiansheng year 9 to Jingyou year 2, within five years Hebei tribute deliveries wastefully spent five million six hundred eighty thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: Zi’s faction added: “Since Shi’s reforms, annual revenue losses are incalculable; comparing Tiansheng 9 through Jingyou 2, Hebei inflated deliveries alone wasted 5.68 million strings in five years;

sentences.zh: 今一旦復用舊法，恐豪商不便，依托權貴，以動朝廷，請先期申諭。

translations.literal: now that the old law is suddenly restored, we fear powerful merchants will be displeased, rely on the powerful and noble to move the court; we request advance proclamation and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: restoring the old rules overnight may anger great merchants who will lobby the powerful—we ask for advance public notice.”

sentences.zh: ”於是帝為下詔戒敕，而縣官濫費自此少矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor issued an edict of admonition, and from then on the state's wasteful spending was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor then issued a warning edict, and treasury waste fell sharply thereafter.

sentences.zh: 久之，上書者復言：“自變法以來，歲輦京師金帛，易芻粟於河北，配擾居民，內虛府庫，外困商旅，非便。

translations.literal: After a long time, memorializers again said: "Since the policy change, each year gold and silks are transported from the capital to exchange for forage and grain in Hebei, requisitioning and harassing residents, emptying the inner treasury and straining outer merchants and travelers—it is not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Years later memorialists again complained: “Since the reforms the court yearly hauls capital gold and silk to swap for Hebei forage, burdening locals, draining the treasury, and squeezing traveling merchants—this helps no one.”

sentences.zh: ”寶元元年，命御史中丞張觀等與三司議之。

translations.literal: " In Baoyuan year 1, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Guan and others were ordered to deliberate with the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Baoyuan 1 (1038) the court ordered Censor-in-Chief Zhang Guan and the Three Departments to review the policy.

sentences.zh: 觀等復請入錢京師以售真州等四務十三場茶，直十萬者，又視景祐三年數損之，為錢六萬七千，入中河北願售茶者，又損一千。

translations.literal: Guan and others again requested paying money at the capital to sell tea from the four offices and thirteen markets such as Zhenzhou; for [tea] valued at one hundred thousand, compared with Jingyou year 3 figures it was further reduced to sixty-seven thousand in money; for Hebei tribute deliveries wishing to sell tea, another reduction of one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guan’s group again proposed capital cash payments for tea from the four offices and thirteen markets: for tea nominally worth 100,000, fees would drop below the Jingyou 3 rate to 67,000 cash, with another 1,000 cut for Hebei deliverers who wanted tea.

sentences.zh: 既而詔又第損二千，於是入錢京師止為錢六萬五千，入中河北為錢六萬四千而已。

translations.literal: Shortly after, an edict further reduced by two thousand in steps; thus payment at the capital was only sixty-five thousand in money, and Hebei tribute delivery only sixty-four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then cut another 2,000 in tiers, leaving capital payments at 65,000 cash and Hebei deliveries at 64,000.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，葉清臣為三司使，是歲河北穀賤，因請內地諸州行三說法，募人入中，且以東南鹽代京師實錢。

translations.literal: In Kangding year 1, Ye Qingchen became Three Departments commissioner; that year grain in Hebei was cheap; he therefore requested that inner circuits' prefectures implement the three-item method, recruiting people for tribute delivery, and also using Southeast salt in place of capital real money.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangding 1 (1040) Ye Qingchen became Three Departments commissioner. With Hebei grain cheap that year, he asked inland prefectures to adopt the three-item method, recruit deliverers, and pay with Southeast salt instead of capital cash.

sentences.zh: 詔糴止二百萬石。

translations.literal: An edict limited purchase to two million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Purchases were capped at two million shi.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，又請募人入芻粟如康定元年法，數足而止，自是三說稍復用矣。

translations.literal: In Qingli year 2, [he] again requested recruiting people to deliver forage and grain as under the Kangding year 1 method, stopping when the quota was met; from this the three-item method was gradually restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 2 (1042) he again recruited forage and grain deliveries under the Kangding 1 rules until quotas were met—and the three-item method slowly returned.

sentences.zh: 八年，三司鹽鐵判官董沔亦請復三說法，三司以為然，因言：“自見錢法行，京師錢入少出多，慶曆七年，榷貨務緡錢入百十九萬，出二百七十六萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Three Departments Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Dong Mian also requested restoring the three-item method; the Three Departments agreed, stating: "Since the cash method was implemented, capital money had more outflow than inflow; in Qingli year 7, the Monopoly Goods Office had one million one hundred ninety thousand strings in and two million seven hundred sixty thousand out.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Salt and Iron Vice Commissioner Dong Mian also urged restoring the three-item method. The Three Departments agreed, noting: “Under the cash method the capital bled money—in Qingli 7 the Monopoly Goods Office took in 1.19 million strings but paid out 2.76 million.

sentences.zh: 以此較之，恐無以贍給，請如沔議，以茶、鹽、香藥、緡錢四物如之。

translations.literal: Comparing by this, we fear there will be no means to supply [needs]; we request following Mian's proposal, using tea, salt, aromatics, and string-cash—four items—in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: At that rate supplies could not be sustained—we ask to follow Mian and use tea, salt, aromatics, and cash as four exchange items.”

sentences.zh: ”於是有四說之法。

translations.literal: " Thereupon there was the four-item method.
translations.idiomatic: ” Thus the four-item method was born.

sentences.zh: 初，詔止行於並邊諸州，而內地諸州有司蓋未嚐請，即以康定元年詔書從事。

translations.literal: At first, the edict was to be implemented only in the border prefectures along Bing; but inner-circuit prefectures' officials had never requested it—they simply followed the Kangding year 1 edict.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was meant only for Bing-border prefectures, yet inland officials who had never asked for it simply applied the Kangding 1 order anyway.

sentences.zh: 自是三說、四說二法並行於河北，不數年間，茶法復壞。

translations.literal: From this the three-item and four-item methods ran in parallel in Hebei; within a few years the tea law again deteriorated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both three-item and four-item methods operated in Hebei together, and within a few years the tea monopoly collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 芻粟之直，大約虛估居十之八，米鬥七百，甚者千錢。

translations.literal: The price of forage and grain was roughly eight-tenths inflated valuation; rice per dou was seven hundred, in severe cases one thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Forged valuations ran to about eighty percent of nominal price; rice reached seven hundred cash per dou, sometimes a thousand.

sentences.zh: 券至京師，為南商所抑，茶每直十萬，止售錢三千，富人乘時收蓄，轉取厚利。

translations.literal: When certificates reached the capital, they were suppressed by southern merchants; tea valued at one hundred thousand each sold for only three thousand in money; the wealthy seized the moment to hoard and resell for thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital southern merchants drove certificates down: tea worth 100,000 fetched only 3,000 cash, while the rich hoarded and flipped them for huge gains.

sentences.zh: 三司患之，請行貼買之法，每券直十萬，比市估三千，倍為六千，復入錢四萬四千，貼為五萬，給茶直十萬。

translations.literal: The Three Departments were troubled by this and requested implementing the supplementary-purchase method: each certificate valued at one hundred thousand, compared with market estimate of three thousand, doubled to six thousand, then paying in another forty-four thousand in money, supplemented to fifty thousand, issuing tea worth one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments, alarmed, proposed supplementary purchase: for each 100,000 certificate worth only 3,000 on the market, double the cash component to 6,000, add another 44,000 for a 50,000 total payment, and issue 100,000 worth of tea.

sentences.zh: 詔又損錢一萬，然亦不足以平其直。

translations.literal: An edict further reduced money by ten thousand, yet this still was insufficient to level the price.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cut another 10,000 cash from the fee, yet prices still would not stabilize.

sentences.zh: 久之，券比售錢三千者，才得二千，往往不售，北商無利，入中者寡，公私大弊。

translations.literal: After a long time, certificates that compared with selling price of three thousand fetched only two thousand, often could not be sold; northern merchants had no profit; tribute deliverers were few; public and private [interests] suffered great harm.
translations.idiomatic: In time certificates that should have brought 3,000 cash sold for barely 2,000 and often not at all; northern merchants saw no profit, few men delivered, and both state and traders suffered.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，知定州韓琦及河北轉運司皆以為言，下三司議。

translations.literal: In Huangyou year 2, Dingzhou prefect Han Qi and the Hebei Transport Commission all spoke on this; the matter was sent down to the Three Departments for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou 2 (1050) Dingzhou prefect Han Qi and the Hebei transport office reported the crisis, and the Three Departments were ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 三司奏：“自改法至今，凡得穀二百二十八萬餘石，芻五十六萬餘圍，而費緡錢一百九十五萬有奇，茶、鹽、香藥又為緡錢一千二百九十五萬有奇。

translations.literal: The Three Departments memorialized: "Since the policy change to now, grain obtained totaled two million two hundred eighty thousand-odd shi, forage fifty-six thousand-odd bundles, while string-cash spent was one million nine hundred fifty thousand-odd; tea, salt, and aromatics [issued] amounted to another one million two hundred ninety-five thousand-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments reported: “Since the reforms we have received 2.28 million shi of grain and 560,000 bundles of forage, but spent 1.95 million strings in cash—while tea, salt, and aromatics issued cost another 12.95 million strings.

sentences.zh: 茶、鹽、香藥，民用有限，榷貨務歲課不過五百萬緡，今散於民間者既多，所在積而不售，故券直亦從而賤。

translations.literal: Tea, salt, and aromatics have limited civilian use; the Monopoly Goods Office's annual revenue does not exceed five million strings; now what is dispersed among the populace is already great; everywhere [goods] accumulate unsold; therefore certificate values also accordingly fall.
translations.idiomatic: Tea, salt, and aromatics have limited civilian demand—the Monopoly Goods Office earns under five million strings a year—yet so much now sits in private hands unsold everywhere that certificate values have collapsed.”

sentences.zh: 茶直十萬，舊錢六萬五千，今止二千；

translations.literal: Tea valued at one hundred thousand formerly [sold for] sixty-five thousand in money; now only two thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Tea worth 100,000 once brought 65,000 cash; now only 2,000;

sentences.zh: 以至香一斤，舊售錢三千八百，今止五六百；

translations.literal: even to aromatics one jin, formerly sold for three thousand eight hundred in money, now only five or six hundred;
translations.idiomatic: fine aromatics once sold for 3,800 cash per jin now fetch five or six hundred;

sentences.zh: 公私兩失其利。

translations.literal: public and private both lost their profit.
translations.idiomatic: state and merchants alike have lost their gain.

sentences.zh: 請復行見錢法，一用景祐三年約束。

translations.literal: We request restoring the cash method, using entirely the Jingyou year 3 regulations.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to restore the cash method under the Jingyou 3 rules alone.”

sentences.zh: ”乃下詔曰：“比食貨法壞，芻粟價益倍，縣官之費日長，商賈不行，豪富之家，乘時牟利，吏緣為奸。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued stating: "Recently the finance and commodities law has broken down; forage and grain prices have more than doubled; state expenses grow daily; merchants and traders do not circulate; wealthy powerful households seize the moment for profit; clerks use this as a pretext for fraud.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor then decreed: “Lately the commodities system has failed: forage prices have doubled, state costs mount daily, trade has stalled, the rich exploit the moment, and clerks turn fraud into routine.

sentences.zh: 自今有議者，須究厥理，審可施用，若事已上而驗問無狀者，置之重罰。

translations.literal: From now on, those who propose [changes] must investigate the principles, carefully determine what can be applied; if a matter has already been submitted and upon verification inquiry proves groundless, impose heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: From now on anyone proposing change must prove the reasoning and show it will work; memorials that fail verification will face severe punishment.”

translations.literal: Close of edict quotation.
translations.idiomatic: The edict concluded.

sentences.zh: 是時雖改見錢法，而京師積錢少，恐不足以支入中之費，帝又出內藏庫錢帛百萬以賜三司。

translations.literal: At this time, although the cash method was changed, accumulated money in the capital was little, and there was fear it would not suffice to cover tribute-delivery expenses; the emperor also disbursed one million in money and silks from the inner treasury to grant the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Although the cash method was restored, capital reserves were thin and might not cover delivery costs; the emperor therefore released one million in cash and silk from the inner treasury for the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 久之，入中者浸多，京師帑藏益乏，商人持券以俟，動彌歲月，至損其直以售於蓄賈之家。

translations.literal: After a long time, tribute deliverers gradually increased; the capital treasury grew ever more depleted; merchants held certificates waiting, often spanning months and years, even cutting their value to sell to hoarding traders.
translations.idiomatic: Over time more men delivered tribute while the capital treasury emptied; merchants waited months or years with certificates, finally discounting them to hoarding wholesalers.

sentences.zh: 言利者請出內藏庫錢稍增價售之，歲可得遺利五十萬緡。

translations.literal: Those who spoke of profit requested disbursing inner-treasury money to slightly raise prices and sell [certificates], annually obtaining surplus profit of five hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Fiscal advocates proposed using inner-treasury cash to bid certificates up slightly, promising five hundred thousand strings in annual surplus.

sentences.zh: 既行，而諫官範鎮謂內藏庫、榷貨務皆領縣官，豈有榷貨務故稽商人，而令內藏乘時射利？

translations.literal: Once implemented, Remonstrance Official Fan Zhen said: "The inner treasury and Monopoly Goods Office both belong to the state treasury—how can the Monopoly Goods Office deliberately delay merchants while the inner treasury seizes the moment for profit?"
translations.idiomatic: Once enacted, remonstrance official Fan Zhen objected: “Both the inner treasury and the Monopoly Goods Office are state agencies—how can one office stall merchants while another speculates for profit?”

sentences.zh: 傷體壞法，莫斯為甚。

translations.literal: Harming the body [of government] and breaking the law—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing could more damage the state’s integrity and its laws.

sentences.zh: 詔即罷之，然自此並邊虛估之弊復起。

translations.literal: An edict immediately abolished it; yet from this time the abuse of inflated valuations along the Bing border arose again.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ended the scheme at once, but inflated valuations along the Bing frontier soon returned.

sentences.zh: 至和三年，河北提舉糴便糧草薛向建議：“並邊十七州軍，歲計粟百八十萬石，為錢百六十萬緡，豆六十五萬石，芻三百七十萬圍，並邊租賦歲可得粟、豆、芻五十萬，其餘皆商人入中。

translations.literal: In Zhihe year 3, Hebei Commissioner for Grain Purchase and Convenient Forage Xue Xiang proposed: "The seventeen prefectures and armies along the Bing border annually require one million eight hundred thousand shi of grain, worth one million six hundred thousand strings, sixty-five thousand shi of beans, three million seven hundred thousand bundles of forage; border rent and tax annually can obtain five hundred thousand [units] of grain, beans, and forage—the rest all comes from merchant tribute delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 3 (1056) Hebei grain commissioner Xue Xiang calculated that the seventeen Bing-border commands needed 1.8 million shi of grain (1.6 million strings), 650,000 shi of beans, and 3.7 million bundles of forage yearly—while border taxes supplied only half a million units combined; merchants delivered the rest.

sentences.zh: 請罷並邊入粟，自京輦錢帛至河北，專以見錢和糴。

translations.literal: We request abolishing Bing-border grain delivery, transporting money and silks from the capital to Hebei, and using only cash for harmonized purchase.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to end Bing-border grain deliveries, haul capital cash and silk to Hebei, and buy grain there with cash alone.”

sentences.zh: ”時楊察為三司使，請用其說。

translations.literal: " At the time Yang Cha was Three Departments commissioner and requested adopting his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: ” Three Departments commissioner Yang Cha endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 因輦絹四十萬匹當緡錢七十萬，又蓄見錢及擇上等茶場八，總為緡錢百五十萬，儲之京師。

translations.literal: Accordingly four hundred thousand bolts of silk were transported, equivalent to seven hundred thousand strings; cash was also stored and eight superior tea markets were selected; totaling one million five hundred thousand strings, stored at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They shipped 400,000 bolts of silk worth 700,000 strings, stockpiled cash, and earmarked eight top tea markets—1.5 million strings in all kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 而募商人入錢並邊，計其道裏遠近，優增其直，以是償之，且省輦運之費，唯入中芻豆計直償以茶如舊。

translations.literal: Merchants were recruited to pay money along the Bing border; calculating distance of routes far and near, valuations were favorably increased to repay them thereby, and transport costs were saved; only for forage and bean tribute delivery were valuations calculated and repaid with tea as before.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants paid cash along the border with premiums scaled to distance, saving haulage costs; only forage and bean deliveries were still repaid in tea at assessed value.

sentences.zh: 行未數年，論者謂輦運科折，煩擾居民，且商人入錢者少，芻豆虛估益高，茶益賤。

translations.literal: Implemented not several years, critics said transport requisitions and apportionments harassed residents; moreover few merchants paid in money; inflated valuations for forage and beans grew ever higher; tea grew ever cheaper.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years critics said transport levies harassed the people, few merchants paid cash, forage valuations inflated further, and tea prices fell still lower.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林學士韓絳等即三司經度。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hanlin Academician Han Jiang and others immediately to survey and plan with the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Hanlin academician Han Jiang and others to review the system with the Three Departments on the spot.

sentences.zh: 絳等言：“自改法以來，邊儲有備，商旅頗通，未宜輕變。

translations.literal: Jiang and others said: "Since the policy change, border stores have been supplied; merchants and travelers circulate fairly well—it is not appropriate to change lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang’s group replied: “Since the reform border stores are stocked and trade flows reasonably well—the policy should not be changed lightly.

sentences.zh: 唯輦運之費，悉從官給，而本路舊輸稅絹者，毋得折為見錢，入中芻豆罷勿給茶，所在平其市估，至京償以銀、綢、絹。

translations.literal: Only transport costs should all be paid from official funds; and for this circuit's former silk-tax payments, they must not be converted to cash; for forage and bean tribute delivery, cease giving tea; locally level market estimates, and at the capital repay with silver, silk gauze, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Only haulage costs should be fully state-paid; silk-tax payments must not be commuted to cash; forage and bean deliveries should no longer receive tea but be valued locally and paid at the capital in silver, gauze, or silk.”

sentences.zh: ”自是茶法不復為邊糴所須，而通商之議起矣。

translations.literal: " From this time the tea law was no longer required for border grain purchase, and debate over free trade arose.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tea was no longer needed to fund border grain purchases, and debate over liberalizing trade began.

sentences.zh: 初，官既榷茶，民私蓄盜販皆有禁，臘茶之禁又嚴於他茶，犯者其罪尤重，凡告捕私茶皆有賞。

translations.literal: At first, once the government monopolized tea, private hoarding and smuggling were all prohibited; prohibition on winter tea was stricter than other teas; offenders' crimes were especially heavy; for all who reported and captured private tea there were rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Once the state monopolized tea, private stockpiling and smuggling were banned outright; winter tea faced even tighter controls and heavier penalties, with rewards for informers.

sentences.zh: 然約束愈密而冒禁愈繁，歲報刑辟，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Yet as regulations grew tighter, violations grew more numerous; annual reports of criminal punishments could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tighter rules bred more violations, and annual criminal cases became uncountable.

sentences.zh: 園戶困於征取，官司並緣侵擾，因陷罪戾至破產逃匿者，歲比有之。

translations.literal: Plantation households were distressed by levies; government offices on all sides encroached and harassed; because of falling into guilt and ruin to bankruptcy and flight, year after year there were such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Plantation households buckled under levies while officials preyed on them; every year some were ruined, convicted, bankrupted, or driven into hiding.

sentences.zh: 又茶法屢變，歲課日削。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the tea law changed repeatedly, and annual revenue daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated policy shifts also eroded annual tea revenue day by day.

sentences.zh: 至和中，歲市茶淮南才四百二十二萬餘斤，江南三百七十五萬餘斤，兩浙二十三萬餘斤，荊湖二百六萬餘斤，唯福建天聖末增至五十萬斤，詔特損五萬，至是增至七十九萬餘斤，歲售錢並本息計之，才百六十七萬二千餘緡。

translations.literal: In Zhihe, annual tea purchased in Huainan was only four million two hundred twenty thousand-odd jin, Jiangnan three million seven hundred fifty thousand-odd jin, Liangzhe two hundred thirty thousand-odd jin, Jinghu two million six hundred thousand-odd jin; only Fujian at the end of Tiansheng had increased to five hundred thousand jin, an edict specially reduced fifty thousand, and by this time it increased to seven hundred ninety thousand-odd jin; annual sales money including principal and interest totaled only one million six hundred seventy-two thousand-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhihe era annual purchases were only 4.22 million jin in Huainan, 3.75 million in Jiangnan, 230,000 in Liangzhe, and 2.6 million in Jinghu; Fujian alone had risen from 500,000 jin at the end of Tiansheng (after a 50,000-jin cut) to 790,000 jin. Total annual receipts, principal and interest included, were just 1.672 million strings.

sentences.zh: 官茶所在陳積，縣官獲利無幾，論者皆謂宜弛禁便。

translations.literal: Official tea everywhere sat aged and piled up; the state gained little profit; commentators all said prohibitions should be relaxed for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Official tea stockpiled everywhere while the treasury gained little; critics agreed the monopoly should be eased.

sentences.zh: 先是，天聖中，有上書者言茶、鹽課虧。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Tiansheng, memorializers said tea and salt revenues were in deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Tiansheng period, memorialists had reported deficits in tea and salt revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝謂執政曰：“茶、鹽，民所食，而強設法以禁之，致犯者眾。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "Tea and salt are what the people consume, yet we forcibly set up laws to prohibit them, causing offenders to be many.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: “Tea and salt are staples of daily life, yet we impose harsh bans and thereby multiply offenders.

sentences.zh: 顧經費尚廣，未能弛禁爾！

translations.literal: But state expenses are still extensive—we cannot yet relax the prohibitions!
translations.idiomatic: But state expenses are still vast—we cannot lift the bans yet!”

sentences.zh: ”景祐中，葉清臣上疏曰：

translations.literal: " During Jingyou, Ye Qingchen submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: ” During Jingyou, Ye Qingchen submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: “山澤有產，天資惠民。

translations.literal: " Mountains and marshes have products—Heaven's endowment to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: “Mountains and marshes yield bounty Heaven meant to enrich the people.

sentences.zh: 兵食不充，財臣兼利，草芽木葉，私不得專，對園置吏，隨處立筦。

translations.literal: When military provisions are insufficient, finance ministers seize profit together; grass sprouts and tree leaves—private persons may not monopolize; facing each garden they place clerks, everywhere establishing barriers.
translations.idiomatic: When armies lack supplies, finance officials seize every profit: even grass sprouts and leaves may not be privately held; clerks are posted at every garden and barriers raised everywhere.

sentences.zh: 一切官禁，人犯則刑，既奪其資，又加之罪，黥流日報，逾冒不悛。

translations.literal: All is government prohibition; if people violate, there is punishment—first seizing their assets, then adding guilt; tattooing and exile are reported daily; exceeding prohibitions without repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Everything is state monopoly: violation brings punishment—first confiscation, then criminal charge; tattooing and exile are reported daily, yet defiance never ends.

sentences.zh: 誠有厚利重貨，能濟國用，聖仁恤隱，矜赦非辜，猶將弛禁緩刑，為民除害。

translations.literal: If there truly were thick profit and heavy goods able to supply state use, the sage's benevolence would pity the hidden, pardon the guiltless—yet still they would relax prohibitions and ease punishments to remove harm for the people.
translations.idiomatic: If the monopoly truly filled the treasury, a sage ruler might still pity the oppressed, pardon the innocent, and ease bans and punishments for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 度支費用甚大，榷易所收甚薄，刳剝園戶，資奉商人，使朝廷有聚斂之名，官曹滋虐濫之罰，虛張名數，刻蠹黎元。

translations.literal: The Revenue Bureau's expenses are very great; monopoly-trade receipts are very thin; gouging plantation households, enriching and supporting merchants—making the court have a name for exaction, official bureaus increase abusive excessive punishments, falsely inflating nominal figures, carving and harming the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Revenue Bureau costs are huge while monopoly receipts are thin: plantation households are flayed to feed merchants, the court earns a reputation for exaction, offices multiply abusive fines, nominal targets are inflated, and common people are carved to the bone.

sentences.zh: 建國以來，法敝輒改，載詳改法之由，非有為國之實，皆商吏協計，倒持利權，幸在更張，倍求奇羨。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the state, whenever the law broke down it was changed; recording in detail the reasons for changing the law—there was no substance of serving the state; all were merchants and clerks in collusion, inverting and holding profit power, fortunate when policies were renewed, doubly seeking extraordinary surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty’s founding, broken laws have been rewritten again and again—yet the records show no true state interest behind the changes, only merchants and clerks colluding, inverting profit to their grip, rejoicing at every reform to double their extraordinary gains.

sentences.zh: 富人豪族，坐以賈贏，薄販下估，日皆朘削，官私之際，俱非遠策。

translations.literal: The wealthy and powerful clans sit on trade profits, slighting sales and lowering estimates; daily all are drained and cut; between state and private—both are not far-sighted policies.
translations.idiomatic: Great clans sit on trade profits, undercut sales and depress valuations, and daily bleed both state and people—no far-sighted policy on either side.

sentences.zh: 臣竊嚐校計茶利所入，以景祐元年為率，除本錢外，實收息錢五十九萬餘緡，又天下所售食茶，並本息歲課亦隻及三十四萬緡，而茶商見通行六十五州軍，所收稅錢已及五十七萬緡。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately tried calculating tea-profit receipts; taking Jingyou year 1 as the standard, apart from capital funds, actual interest money received was five hundred ninety thousand-odd strings; furthermore, all beverage tea sold empire-wide, including principal and interest, annual revenue also reached only three hundred forty thousand strings; yet tea merchants currently circulate through sixty-five prefectures and armies, and tax money collected already reached five hundred seventy thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: I have reckoned tea revenue using Jingyou 1 as the benchmark: aside from capital costs, actual interest was only 590,000 strings; empire-wide beverage-tea sales, principal and interest included, yielded just 340,000 strings—yet tea merchants already trade through sixty-five commands and pay 570,000 strings in taxes.

sentences.zh: 若令天下通商，隻收稅錢，自及數倍，即榷務、山場及食茶之利，盡可籠取。

translations.literal: If the empire were ordered to permit free trade and only collect tax money, it would naturally reach several times that amount; then the profits of monopoly offices, mountain stations, and beverage tea could all be encompassed and taken.
translations.idiomatic: If trade were opened empire-wide and only taxes collected, receipts would naturally multiply several times over—encompassing every profit now taken at monopoly offices, mountain stations, and beverage-tea sales.

sentences.zh: 又況不費度支之本，不置榷易之官，不興輦運之勞，不濫徒黥之辟。

translations.literal: Moreover, not spending Revenue Bureau capital, not establishing monopoly-trade officials, not raising transport labor, not abusing exile and tattooing punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the state would spend no Revenue Bureau capital, employ no monopoly officers, impose no transport levies, and inflict no flood of tattooing and exile.

sentences.zh: 臣意生民之弊，有時而窮，盛德之事，俟聖不惑。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the people's harms have times when they reach their limit; matters of great virtue await the sage's unconfused [judgment].
translations.idiomatic: I believe the people's suffering must someday reach its limit, and a matter of true virtue awaits a sage ruler's clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 議者謂榷賣有定率，征稅無彝準，通商之後，必虧歲計。

translations.literal: Critics say monopoly sale has fixed rates, while taxation has no constant standard; after free trade, annual accounts will surely be in deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say monopoly sales have fixed rates whereas taxes lack a steady standard, and free trade would surely shrink the annual budget.

sentences.zh: 臣按管氏鹽鐵法，計口受賦，茶為人用，與鹽鐵均，必令天下通行，以口定賦，民獲善利，又去嚴刑，口數出錢，人不厭取。

translations.literal: Your servant examines Guanzi's salt-and-iron law: calculating per mouth to receive levies. Tea is used by people, equal to salt and iron—it must be ordered that the empire circulate freely, fixing levies by population; the people obtain good profit, and severe punishments are also removed; by mouth-count paying money, people will not resent the levy.
translations.idiomatic: I follow Guanzi’s salt-and-iron model of per-capita levy: tea, like salt and iron, is a daily necessity. Let it circulate freely empire-wide, tax by headcount, let the people prosper, end harsh punishments, and charge a per-person fee the public will not resent.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，天下戶千二十九萬六千五百六十五，丁二千六百二十萬五千四百四十一，三分其一為產茶州軍，內外郭鄉又居三分之一，丁賦錢三十，村鄉丁賦二十，不產茶州軍郭鄉村鄉如前計之，又第損十錢，歲計已及緡錢四十萬。

translations.literal: In Jingyou year 1, empire-wide households numbered 10,296,565 and adult males 26,205,441; one-third of these were in tea-producing prefectures and armies; of urban wards and rural townships within and without [the walls], another third [were counted]; the adult-male levy was thirty cash, the village-and-township levy twenty; in non-tea prefectures, urban and rural [levies] were calculated as before, then further reduced by ten cash per step—the annual total already reached four hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 1 (1034), the empire had 10,296,565 households and 26,205,441 adult males. One-third lived in tea-producing circuits; of urban and rural districts, another third were included. The levy was thirty cash per adult male and twenty in villages and townships; non-tea circuits used the same formula with a further ten-cash reduction at each tier—yielding about four hundred thousand strings per year.

sentences.zh: 榷茶之利，凡止九十餘萬緡，通商收稅，且以三倍舊稅為率，可得一百七十餘萬緡，更加口賦之入，乃有二百一十餘萬緡，或更於收稅則例，微加增益，即所增至寡，所聚愈厚，比於官自榷易，驅民就刑，利病相須，炳然可察。

translations.literal: The profit from tea monopoly in all amounted to only nine hundred thousand-odd strings; with open trade collecting tax, taking triple the old tax as the rate, one could obtain one million seven hundred thousand-odd strings; adding the income from per-capita levies, there would be two million one hundred thousand-odd strings; or if in the tax-collection regulations one slightly increased, though the increase would be small, what was gathered would grow thicker—compared with the government itself monopolizing and trading, driving the people toward punishment, benefit and harm mutually dependent, clearly observable.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly tea revenue totaled barely nine hundred thousand strings. Under free trade taxed at triple the old rate, receipts could reach 1.7 million; add the head tax and the total would exceed 2.1 million. Even a modest rate tweak would swell collections—whereas official monopoly drove commoners into the courts. The trade-off was plain.

sentences.zh: ”時下三司議，皆以為不可行。

translations.literal: " At that time the Three Departments deliberated, and all deemed it unfeasible.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Three Departments then reviewed the plan and unanimously judged it unworkable.

sentences.zh: 至嘉祐中，著作佐郎何鬲、三班奉職王嘉麟又皆上書請罷給茶本錢，縱園戶貿易，而官收租錢與所在征算，歸榷貨務以償邊糴之費，可以疏利源而寬民力。

translations.literal: By the Jiayou period, Associate Editorial Gentleman He Ge and Third-Class Service Attendant Wang Jialin again each submitted memorials requesting abolition of issued tea capital funds, allowing plantation households free trade, while the government collected rent money and local transit levies, returning [proceeds] to the Monopoly Goods Office to repay border grain-purchase costs—thereby able to broaden profit sources and ease the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiayou (1056–1063), Associate Editorial Gentleman He Ge and Third-Class Service Attendant Wang Jialin each petitioned to end government tea advances, let growers trade freely, and fund border grain purchases through rent and transit taxes paid into the Monopoly Goods Office—widening revenue while easing the public burden.

sentences.zh: 嘉麟為《登平致頌書》十卷、《隆衍視成策》二卷上之，淮南轉運副使沈立亦集《茶法利害》為十卷，陳通商之利。

translations.literal: Jialin composed Ten Scrolls of "Ascending Peace and Offering Praise" and Two Scrolls of "Grand Extension and Gazing on Completion" and presented them; Huainan Transport Vice Commissioner Shen Li also compiled Ten Scrolls of "Advantages and Harms of the Tea Law," setting forth the benefits of open trade.
translations.idiomatic: Jialin submitted ten scrolls entitled Ascending Peace and Offering Praise and two scrolls entitled Grand Extension and Gazing on Completion; Huainan transport vice commissioner Shen Li also compiled ten scrolls on the tea law’s costs and benefits, arguing for free trade.

sentences.zh: 時富弼、韓琦、曾公亮執政，決意向之，力言於帝。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Zeng Gongliang held power; their resolve inclined toward it, and they spoke forcefully to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Zeng Gongliang were then in charge, firmly favored reform, and pressed the emperor at length.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，命韓絳、陳升之、呂景初即三司置局議之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of year 3, [the court] ordered Han Jiang, Chen Shengzhi, and Lü Jingchu to establish a bureau at the Three Departments to deliberate it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Jiayou 3 (1058), Han Jiang, Chen Shengzhi, and Lü Jingchu were ordered to set up a Three Departments bureau to study the change.

sentences.zh: 十月，三司言：“茶課緡錢歲當入二百二十四萬八千，嘉祐二年才及一百二十八萬，又募人入錢，皆有虛數，實為八十六萬，而三十九萬有奇是為本錢，才得子錢四十六萬九千，而輦運麋耗喪失，與官吏、兵夫廩給雜費，又不預焉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Three Departments said: "Tea-duty strings in money annually ought to enter 2,248,000; in Jiayou year 2 it reached only 1,280,000; furthermore recruiting people to pay in money—all had inflated figures; in reality it was 860,000, while three hundred ninety thousand-odd was capital funds, obtaining only 469,000 in interest money; yet transport wear, loss, and the miscellaneous expenses of officials, soldiers, and grain rations were still not included.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Three Departments reported: “Annual tea revenue should be 2,248,000 strings; in Jiayou 2 it barely reached 1,280,000, and much of that was inflated. Net receipts were really 860,000, of which 390,000 was principal—only 469,000 profit—while transport losses and official, soldier, and ration costs were not even counted.

sentences.zh: 至於園戶輸納，侵擾日甚，小民趨利犯法，刑辟益繁，獲利至少，為弊甚大。

translations.literal: As for plantation households' delivery, harassment daily grew worse; petty people rushed profit and violated law; penal statutes increased ever more; profit obtained was least, while abuses were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Growers faced ever worse exactions; petty cultivators broke the law chasing profit; punishments multiplied; profits shrank while abuses ballooned.

sentences.zh: 宜約至和以後一歲之數，以所得息錢均賦茶民，恣其買賣，所在收算，請遣官詢察利害以聞。

translations.literal: It is fitting to take the figures from one year after Zhihe and afterward, use the interest money obtained to distribute equally among tea commoners, let them buy and sell freely, collect transit levies locally, and request dispatching officials to inquire into advantages and harms and report.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed averaging one post-Zhihe year’s interest across all tea growers, freeing trade, levying transit taxes locally, and sending officials to report on the results.

sentences.zh: ”詔遣官分行六路，還言如三司使議便。

translations.literal: " An edict dispatched officials to proceed in six circuits; on return they said the Three Departments commissioner’s plan was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: ” The throne sent commissioners through six circuits; on their return all endorsed the Three Departments plan.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，詔曰：“古者山澤之利，與民共之，故民足於下，而君裕於上，國家無事，刑罰以清。

translations.literal: In the second month of year 4, an edict stated: "In antiquity the profit of mountains and marshes was shared with the people; therefore the people were sufficient below while the ruler was ample above; the state had no affairs, and punishments were clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Jiayou 4 (1059) an edict declared: “In antiquity mountain and marsh bounty was shared with the people, so the populace prospered below and the ruler was secure above; the realm was tranquil and punishments few.

sentences.zh: 自唐建中時，始有茶禁，上下規利，垂二百年。

translations.literal: From the Jianzhong era of Tang, there began tea prohibition; above and below schemed for profit—nearly two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Tea bans began in Tang’s Jianzhong era (780s); for nearly two centuries court and people alike chased monopoly profit.

sentences.zh: 如聞比來為患益甚，民被誅求之困，日惟谘嗟，官受濫惡之入，歲以陳積，私藏盜販，犯者實繁，嚴刑重誅，情所不忍，是於江湖之間幅員數千里，為陷阱以害吾民也。

translations.literal: As heard, recently the harm has grown especially severe: the people suffer the distress of exaction and daily only sigh; the government receives tainted, inferior intake yearly piled in store; private hoarding and illicit sale—violators truly numerous; severe punishments and heavy executions—the sentiment cannot bear it; this is, across thousands of li between rivers and lakes, making a trap to harm our people.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the harm has worsened: the people groan under exaction while the state stockpiles shoddy tea; smuggling flourishes and punishments are cruel beyond endurance—we have turned thousands of li along the rivers and lakes into a trap for our own subjects.

sentences.zh: 朕心惻然，念此久矣，間遣使者往就問之，而皆歡然願弛其禁，歲入之課以時上官。

translations.literal: Our heart has been sorrowful, thinking on this long; occasionally dispatching envoys to go and inquire, and all joyfully wished to relax the prohibition, with annual revenue duties presented to superiors on time.
translations.idiomatic: We have long grieved over this and sent envoys to inquire; everywhere the people gladly asked for an end to the ban and promised timely payment of the annual duty.

sentences.zh: 一二近臣，條析其狀，朕猶若慊然，又於歲輸裁減其數，使得饒阜，以相為生，俾通商利。

translations.literal: One or two close ministers analyzed the situation; We still felt as if insufficient, and again in annual delivery trimmed the figures, enabling abundance and plenty, mutually to sustain life, and thereby to open commercial profit.
translations.idiomatic: After close ministers analyzed the figures We still felt the burden too heavy, cut the annual quota further so the people could recover, and opened the way to free trade.

sentences.zh: 曆世之敝，一旦以除，著為經常，弗復更製，損上益下，以休吾民。

translations.literal: Abuses of successive ages—on one morning removed; established as constant regulation, no further changes; reducing above and benefiting below, to rest Our people.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses of ages were swept away in a day, fixed as permanent law, never to be reversed—sacrificing revenue to give Our people rest.

sentences.zh: 尚慮喜於立異之人、緣而為奸之黨，妄陳奏議，以惑官司，必置明刑，無或有貸。

translations.literal: Still fearing people who delight in proposing novelties and factions who seize the occasion to commit wrong, rashly submitting memorials to confuse the offices—definite severe punishments shall be applied, without any pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet We warn those who love novelty and factions that would abuse the change: whoever rashly petitions to overturn this policy will face stern punishment without mercy.

translations.literal: Close of edict quotation.
translations.idiomatic: The edict concluded.

sentences.zh: 初，所遣官既議弛禁，因以三司歲課均賦茶戶，凡為緡錢六十八萬有奇，使歲輸縣官。

translations.literal: Initially, the dispatched officials having deliberated relaxing the prohibition, thereby took the Three Departments' annual duty and distributed it equally among tea households—altogether four hundred eighty thousand-odd strings in money—making them pay annually to the county government.
translations.idiomatic: When the commissioners first planned to lift the ban, they spread the Three Departments’ annual tea quota—about 680,000 strings—across all tea households as a yearly payment to local government.

sentences.zh: 比輸茶時，其出幾倍，朝廷難之，為損其半，歲輸緡錢三十三萬八千有奇，謂之租錢，與諸路本錢悉儲以待邊糴。

translations.literal: When compared with [what they would pay] delivering tea, the outlay was several times [greater]; the court found it difficult and halved it; annual delivery was three hundred thirty-eight thousand-odd strings in money, called rent money; with principal funds of each circuit all stored to await border grain purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Cash payment proved several times costlier than delivering tea, so the court halved the assessment to 338,000-odd strings, termed “rent money,” with circuit principal funds banked for border grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 自是唯臘茶禁如舊，餘茶肆行天下矣。

translations.literal: From this time only the prohibition on wax tea remained as before; the rest of tea freely circulated throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth only the wax-tea monopoly remained; all other tea could trade freely empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 論者猶謂朝廷誌於恤人，欲省刑罰，其意良善；

translations.literal: Discussants still said the court's aim lay in cherishing the people and wishing to reduce punishments—the intent was truly good;
translations.idiomatic: Critics conceded the court meant to spare the people and reduce punishments—a worthy aim;

sentences.zh: 然茶戶困於輸錢，而商賈利薄，販鬻者少，州縣征稅日蹙，經費不充，學士劉敞、歐陽修頗論其事。

translations.literal: yet tea households were distressed by paying money, while merchants' profit was thin and sellers few; prefecture and county tax collection daily tightened; funds were insufficient; Academician Liu Chang and Ouyang Xiu discussed the matter at length.
translations.idiomatic: yet growers struggled under cash levies, merchant margins thinned, sales fell, and local tax receipts shrank. Academician Liu Chang and Ouyang Xiu both analyzed the fallout.

sentences.zh: 敞疏大要以謂先時百姓之摘山者，受錢於官，而今也顧使之納錢於官，受納之間，利害百倍；

translations.literal: Chang's memorial's main points held that formerly common people who picked mountains received money from the government, whereas now they are made to pay money to the government—between receiving and paying, benefit and harm differ a hundredfold;
translations.idiomatic: Chang’s memorial chiefly argued that mountain pickers once received state advances but now paid the state—inverting the flow multiplied the harm a hundredfold;

sentences.zh: 先時百姓冒法販茶者被罰耳，今悉均賦於民，賦不時入，刑亦及之，是良民代冒法者受罪；

translations.literal: formerly common people who illicitly sold tea in violation of law were punished only; now all are equally assessed on the people—if the assessment is not paid in time, punishment also reaches them: this is making good commoners suffer punishment in place of lawbreakers;
translations.idiomatic: once only smugglers were punished; now every household owes a quota, and late payment brings criminal sanction—law-abiding subjects pay for smugglers’ crimes;

sentences.zh: 先時大商富賈為國懋遷，而州郡收其稅，今大商富賈不行，則稅額不登，且乏國用。

translations.literal: formerly great merchants and rich traders made grand removals for the state while prefectures and counties collected their tax; now if great merchants and rich traders do not travel, then tax quotas are not registered, and state use is also lacking.
translations.idiomatic: once great merchants moved goods nationwide and localities collected transit tax; now that they stayed home, transit revenue collapsed and the treasury suffered.

sentences.zh: 修言新法之行，一利而有五害，大略與敞意同。

translations.literal: Xiu said the new law's implementation had one benefit but five harms—broadly the same as Chang's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu judged the reform one gain against five losses—substantially Chang’s view.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方排眾論而行之，敞等雖言，不聽也。

translations.literal: At that time the court was just rejecting diverse opinion to implement it; though Chang and others spoke, [the court] did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The court pressed ahead over opposition; Chang and his allies were ignored.

sentences.zh: 治平中，歲入臘茶四十八萬九千餘斤，散茶二十五萬五千餘斤，茶戶租錢三十二萬九千八百五十五緡，又儲本錢四十七萬四千三百二十一緡，而內外總入茶稅錢四十九萬八千六百緡，推是可見茶法得失矣。

translations.literal: During Zhiping, annual intake of wax tea was four hundred eighty-nine thousand-odd jin, loose tea two hundred fifty-five thousand-odd jin; tea-household rent money three hundred twenty-nine thousand eight hundred fifty-five strings; also stored principal funds four hundred seventy-four thousand three hundred twenty-one strings; while inner and outer total tea-tax money intake was four hundred ninety-eight thousand six hundred strings—pushing from this, tea-law gain and loss can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhiping (1064–1067) wax tea receipts were 489,000-odd jin and loose tea 255,000-odd jin; grower rent yielded 329,855 strings; stored principal totaled 474,321 strings; empire-wide tea tax brought 498,600 strings—figures enough to show how the law fared.

sentences.zh: 自天聖以來，茶法屢易，嘉祐始行通商，雖議者或以為不便，而更法之意則主於優民。

translations.literal: From Tiansheng onward, the tea law changed repeatedly; Jiayou first implemented open trade—though discussants sometimes deemed it inconvenient, the intent of changing the law chiefly lay in benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tiansheng the tea law had shifted often; Jiayou inaugurated free trade. Critics found fault, but reformers aimed chiefly to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，神宗與大臣論昔茶法之弊，文彥博、吳充、王安石各論其故，然於茶法未有所變。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, Shenzong with great ministers discussed the abuses of the former tea law; Wen Yanbo, Wu Chong, and Wang Anshi each discussed the reasons, yet regarding the tea law there was no change.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 4 (1071) Shenzong reviewed past tea-policy failures with his ministers; Wen Yanbo, Wu Chong, and Wang Anshi each explained the causes, but the law itself was not altered.

sentences.zh: 及王韶建開湟之策，委以經略。

translations.literal: When Wang Shao proposed the policy of opening the Huang [River region], [the court] entrusted him with frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao advanced his plan to open the Huang frontier, the court gave him strategic command.

sentences.zh: 七年，始遣三司幹當公事李杞入蜀經畫買茶，於秦鳳、熙河博馬。

translations.literal: In year 7, it first dispatched Three Departments Duty Officer Li Qi to enter Shu to plan tea purchase, and at Qin-Feng and Xi-He to exchange for horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 (1074) the court first sent Three Departments duty officer Li Qi into Sichuan to organize tea purchases for horse trade at Qin-Feng and Xi-He.

sentences.zh: 而韶言西人頗以善馬至邊，所嗜唯茶，乏茶與市。

translations.literal: Shao said western people quite often brought good horses to the border; what they desired was only tea—lacking tea, they would not trade.
translations.idiomatic: Shao reported that western peoples brought fine horses to the border but would trade only for tea—without tea, no deal.

sentences.zh: 即詔趨趣杞據見茶計水陸運致，又以銀十萬兩、帛二萬五千、度僧牒五百付之，假常平及坊場餘錢，以著作佐郎蒲宗閔同領其事。

translations.literal: Immediately an edict urged Qi according to visible tea to plan water-and-land transport delivery; also one hundred thousand liang of silver, twenty-five thousand bolts of silk, and five hundred ordination certificates were given him; borrowing Ever-Normal and market-yard surplus funds; with Associate Editorial Gentleman Pu Zongmin jointly to lead the affair.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Qi to rush available tea by land and water, advanced 100,000 liang of silver, 25,000 bolts of silk, and 500 ordination certificates, and lent Ever-Normal and market-yard reserves, with Associate Editorial Gentleman Pu Zongmin as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 初，蜀之茶園，皆民兩稅地，不殖五穀，唯宜種茶。

translations.literal: Initially, Shu's tea gardens were all on the people's dual-tax land; they did not plant the five grains—only tea planting was suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan’s tea gardens stood on land already subject to the two-tax levy; grain would not grow there—only tea thrived.

sentences.zh: 賦稅一例折輸，蓋為錢三百，折輸綢絹皆一匹；

translations.literal: Tax levies were uniformly commuted: roughly three hundred cash commuted to one bolt of silk or damask each;
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were commuted in fixed equivalents: about three hundred cash per bolt of silk or damask;

sentences.zh: 若為錢十，則折輸綿一兩；

translations.literal: if ten cash, then commuted to one liang of cotton;
translations.idiomatic: ten cash to one liang of cotton;

sentences.zh: 為錢二，則折輸草一圍。

translations.literal: if two cash, then commuted to one bundle of fodder grass.
translations.idiomatic: two cash to one bundle of fodder grass.

sentences.zh: 役錢亦視其賦。

translations.literal: Corvée money also followed their levy.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée payments followed the same scale.

sentences.zh: 民賣茶資衣食，與農夫業田無異，而稅額總三十萬。

translations.literal: The people sold tea to support clothing and food—no different from farmers' tilling fields—yet the tax quota in total was three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tea sales clothed and fed them like farming, yet total tax assessments ran to three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 杞被命經度，又詔得調舉官屬，乃即屬諸州創設官場，歲增息為四十萬，而重禁榷之令。

translations.literal: Qi received orders to plan; again an edict permitted him to transfer and recommend office subordinates; thereupon in subordinate prefectures he newly established government markets, annually increasing interest by four hundred thousand, and again heavily prohibited monopoly orders.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to reorganize the trade, Qi could recruit staff, set up government tea markets in subordinate prefectures, raise annual profit by four hundred thousand strings, and reimpose strict monopoly enforcement.

sentences.zh: 其輸受之際，往往厭其斤重，侵其價直，法既加急矣。

translations.literal: At the time of delivery and receipt, they often disliked the jin weight and encroached on the price value—the law had already grown urgent.
translations.idiomatic: At delivery officials often short-weighted purchases and shaved prices—the regime had already turned harsh.

sentences.zh: 八年，杞以疾去。

translations.literal: In year 8, Qi left due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Qi resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 先是，杞等歲增十萬之息，既而運茶積滯，歲課不給，即建畫於彭、漢二州歲買布各十萬匹，以折腳費，實以布息助茶利，然茶亦未免積滯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi and others annually increased interest by one hundred thousand; afterward tea transport piled up stagnant, and annual duties could not be met; thereupon they planned at Peng and Han two prefectures annually to buy one hundred thousand bolts of cloth each to cover transport shortfall—actually using cloth interest to assist tea profit—yet tea still could not avoid stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Qi’s team had boosted annual profit by one hundred thousand, but tea then backed up and quotas failed; they arranged for Peng and Han to buy one hundred thousand bolts of cloth each yearly to cover transport costs—cloth profits subsidizing tea—yet tea still piled up unsold.

sentences.zh: 都官郎中劉佐復議歲易解鹽十萬席，顧運回車船載入蜀，而禁商販，蓋恐布亦難敷也。

translations.literal: Capital Bureau Director Liu Zuo again proposed annually exchanging one hundred thousand bundles of solution salt, intending to use returning carts and boats to carry it into Shu, while prohibiting merchant trade—probably fearing cloth also would be hard to distribute.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Bureau director Liu Zuo proposed trading in one hundred thousand bundles of solution salt yearly, shipping it into Sichuan on return convoys while banning private merchants—fearing cloth alone could not cover costs.

sentences.zh: 詔既以佐代杞，未幾，鹽法復難行，遂罷佐。

translations.literal: An edict having replaced Qi with Zuo, before long the salt law again proved hard to implement, and Zuo was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo replaced Qi by edict, but the salt scheme soon failed and Zuo was removed.

sentences.zh: 而宗閔乃議川峽路民茶息收什之三，盡賣於官場，更嚴私交易之令，稍重至徒刑，仍沒緣身所有物，以待賞給。

translations.literal: Zongmin then proposed that Sichuan-Canyon circuit people's tea interest be collected at three-tenths, entirely sold to government markets; private trade prohibitions were made stricter, in serious cases reaching penal servitude, still confiscating all goods on the person to await reward distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin then proposed taxing Sichuan tea profits at thirty percent, forcing all sales through government markets, tightening private-trade bans to penal servitude with confiscation of offenders’ goods for informer rewards.

sentences.zh: 於是蜀茶盡榷，民始病焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shu tea was entirely monopolized, and the people first suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan tea was fully monopolized, and the populace first felt the pain.

sentences.zh: 十年，知彭州呂陶言：“川峽四路所出茶，比東南十不及一，諸路既許通商，兩川卻為禁地，虧損治體。

translations.literal: In year 10, Pengzhou prefect Lü Tao said: "The tea produced in the four circuits of Chuan-Xia amounts to less than one-tenth of the southeast; the various circuits already permit open trade, yet the two Shu [regions] are a prohibited zone—damaging the principle of governance.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Pengzhou prefect Lü Tao argued: “Tea from the four Sichuan circuits is less than a tenth of the southeast’s output; free trade is allowed elsewhere, yet both Shu regions remain closed—a breach of good governance.

sentences.zh: 如解州有鹽池，民間煎者乃是私鹽，晉州有礬山，民間煉者乃是私礬，今川蜀茶園，皆百姓己物，與解鹽、晉礬不同。

translations.literal: For example, Jiezhou has a salt pond—what the people boil is private salt; Jinzhou has an alum mountain—what the people smelt is private alum; but now Chuan-Shu tea gardens are all the common people's own property, different from Jie salt and Jin alum.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhou’s salt pond and Jinzhou’s alum hill involve state resources illicitly worked; Sichuan’s tea gardens are ordinary household property—quite unlike Jie salt or Jin alum.

sentences.zh: 又市易司籠製百貨，歲出息錢不過十之二，然必以一年為率；

translations.literal: Furthermore the Market Exchange Office monopolizes all goods; annual interest money does not exceed two-tenths, yet it must take one year as the rate;
translations.idiomatic: The Market Exchange Office, which monopolizes general merchandise, takes barely twenty percent annual interest on a one-year basis;

sentences.zh: 今茶場司務重立法，盡榷民茶，隨買隨賣，取息十之三，或今日買十千之茶，明日即作十三千賣之，變轉不休，比至歲終，豈止三分？

translations.literal: now the Tea Market Office heavily legislates anew, entirely monopolizing people's tea, buying as sold and taking interest of three-tenths—or if today buying ten thousand's worth of tea, tomorrow marking it up to thirteen thousand for sale, turning over without cease: compared to year-end, how is it only three-tenths?
translations.idiomatic: yet the Tea Market Office monopolizes all private tea, buying and reselling at thirty percent markup—ten thousand today, thirteen thousand tomorrow, turnover endless—far more than thirty percent by year’s end.

sentences.zh: ”因奏劉佐、李杞、蒲宗閔等苟希進用，必欲出息三分，致茶戶被害。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he memorialized that Liu Zuo, Li Qi, Pu Zongmin, and others, hoping for advancement, necessarily wished to obtain three-tenths interest, causing tea households to suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: ” He charged Liu Zuo, Li Qi, Pu Zongmin, and others with courting promotion by squeezing thirty percent interest from growers.

sentences.zh: 始詔息止收十之一，佐坐措置乖方罷，以國子博士李稷代之，而陶亦得罪。

translations.literal: Initially an edict limited interest to one-tenth; Zuo was dismissed for maladministration; Guozijian Doctor Li Ji replaced him, while Tao also suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court first capped interest at ten percent; Zuo was dismissed for mismanagement; Guozijian doctor Li Ji replaced him, and Tao was punished.

sentences.zh: 稷依李杞例兼三司判官，仍委權不限員舉劾。

translations.literal: Ji followed Li Qi's precedent as concurrent Three Departments judge, still entrusted with authority to impeach without limit on personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ji held a concurrent Three Departments judgeship like Qi and received unlimited impeachment authority.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周尹論蜀中榷茶為民害，罷為提點湖北刑獄。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Zhou Yin discussed that monopoly tea in Shu was a harm to the people and was dismissed to be Huabei Circuit judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Zhou Yin denounced Sichuan’s tea monopoly as a public harm and was transferred to judicial intendant of Hubei circuit.

sentences.zh: 利州路漕臣張宗諤、張升卿議廢茶場司，依舊通商，詔付稷，稷方以茶利要功，言宗諤等所陳皆疏謬，罪當無赦。

translations.literal: Lizhou circuit transport officials Zhang Zong'e and Zhang Shengqing proposed abolishing the Tea Market Office and restoring open trade as before; an edict referred it to Ji; Ji, just then using tea profit to demand merit, said Zong'e and others' statements were all crude errors, guilt deserving no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou transport officials Zhang Zong’e and Zhang Shengqing urged abolishing the Tea Market Office and restoring free trade; the memorial went to Ji, who—seeking credit from tea profits—called their views absurd and unpardonable.

sentences.zh: 雖會赦，猶皆坐貶秩二等。

translations.literal: Although an amnesty occurred, all still suffered demotion by two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Despite a general amnesty, both were still demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 於是稷建議賣茶官非材，許對易，如闕員，於前資待闕官差；

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji proposed that tea-selling officials lacking talent be permitted exchange appointments; if posts were vacant, former qualified officials awaiting appointment would be sent;
translations.idiomatic: Ji then allowed unqualified tea-market officials to be replaced by exchange appointment and vacant posts filled from the senior waiting list;

sentences.zh: 茶場司事，州郡毋得越職聽治。

translations.literal: Tea Market Office affairs—prefectures and counties must not overstep office to hear and decide.
translations.idiomatic: and barred prefectures and counties from interfering in Tea Market Office business.

sentences.zh: 又以茶價增減或不一，裁立中價，定歲入課額，及設酬賞以待官吏，而三路三十六場大小使臣並不限員。

translations.literal: Also because tea prices when increased or reduced were not uniform, a median price was cut and established, fixing annual revenue quotas, and setting rewards to await officials; the three circuits' thirty-six markets' great and small envoys and commissioners were also without personnel limits.
translations.idiomatic: Because tea prices fluctuated, he set a median price, fixed annual quotas, offered official rewards, and staffed thirty-six markets across three circuits without personnel caps.

sentences.zh: 重園戶采造黃花秋葉茶之禁，犯者沒官。

translations.literal: He heavily prohibited plantation households from producing yellow-flower and autumn-leaf tea; violators' [goods] were confiscated by the government.
translations.idiomatic: He banned growers from making yellow-flower and autumn-leaf tea on pain of confiscation.

sentences.zh: 蒲宗閔亦援稷比，許舉劾官吏，以重其權，二人皆務浚利刻急。

translations.literal: Pu Zongmin also followed Ji's precedent, permitted to impeach officials to strengthen his authority—the two men both strove to dredge profit and be harshly urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zongmin likewise received impeachment powers like Ji; both men pursued profit ruthlessly.

sentences.zh: 茶場監官買茶精良及滿五千馱以及萬馱，第賞有差，而所買粗惡偽濫者，計虧坐贓論。

translations.literal: Tea-market supervising officials who bought fine tea and reached five thousand loads or up to ten thousand loads received graded rewards by rank; those who bought coarse, inferior, or adulterated [tea]—calculating loss—were judged under embezzlement statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Market supervisors who bought fine tea in quantities of five or ten thousand loads earned graded bonuses; those who bought coarse or adulterated tea were prosecuted for embezzlement by the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 凡茶場州軍知州、通判並兼提舉，經略使所在，即委通判。

translations.literal: In all, for tea-market prefectures and armies, prefects and vice-prefects concurrently supervised; where a frontier commissioner was stationed, it was entrusted to the vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and vice-prefects concurrently oversaw tea markets; where a frontier commissioner resided, the vice-prefect took charge.

sentences.zh: 又禁南入熙河、秦鳳、涇原路，如私販臘茶法。

translations.literal: Also prohibited southward entry into Xi-He, Qin-Feng, and Jingyuan circuits—as with the private-sale wax-tea law.
translations.idiomatic: Southward shipment into Xi-He, Qin-Feng, and Jingyuan was banned under the same rules as illicit wax-tea trade.

sentences.zh: 五年，李稷死永樂城，詔以陸師閔代之。

translations.literal: In year 5, Li Ji died at Yongle Fort; an edict replaced him with Lu Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Li Ji died at Yongle Fort; Lu Shimin succeeded him by edict.

sentences.zh: 師閔言稷治茶五年，百費外獲淨息四百二十八萬餘緡，詔賜田十頃。

translations.literal: Shimin said that in five years of Ji's managing tea, apart from all expenses, net interest obtained was four million two hundred eighty thousand-odd strings; an edict bestowed ten qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin reported that in five years Ji had cleared 4.28 million strings net after all costs; the throne rewarded him with ten qing of land.

sentences.zh: 而師閔榷利，尤刻於前，建言：“文、階州接連，而茶法不同，階為禁地，有博馬、賣茶場，文獨為通商地。

translations.literal: Shimin's monopoly profit was especially harsh compared with before; he submitted saying: "Wen and Jie prefectures are adjacent, yet tea laws differ: Jie is a prohibited zone, with horse-exchange and tea-selling markets; Wen alone is open-trade territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin’s monopoly was harsher still. He noted that adjacent Wen and Jie prefectures followed different rules: Jie was closed, with horse and tea markets, while Wen remained open to merchants.

sentences.zh: 乞文、龍二州並禁榷；

translations.literal: We request that Wen and Long two prefectures also be placed under prohibition monopoly;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Wen and Long be placed under monopoly as well;

sentences.zh: 仍許川路餘羨茶貨入陝西變賣，於成都府置博賣都茶場。

translations.literal: still permit Sichuan circuit surplus tea goods to enter Shaanxi for resale, and at Chengdu Prefecture establish a general monopoly tea-selling market.
translations.idiomatic: allow surplus Sichuan tea into Shaanxi for resale, and establish a central monopoly sales market at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: ”事皆施行。

translations.literal: " The matters were all implemented.
translations.idiomatic: ” All were approved.

sentences.zh: 初，群牧判官郭茂恂言，賣茶買馬，事實相須，詔茂恂同提舉茶場。
