translations.literal: Initially, Herd Administration Judge Guo Maoxun said selling tea to buy horses—the affairs in fact mutually depended; an edict ordered Maoxun jointly to supervise tea markets.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Herd Administration judge Guo Maoxun had argued that tea sales and horse purchases were inseparable; he was ordered to co-supervise tea markets.

sentences.zh: 至是，師閔以買馬司兼領茶場，茶法不能自立，詔罷買馬司兼領；

translations.literal: By this time Shimin, with the Horse-Purchase Office concurrently leading tea markets, the tea law could not stand on its own; an edict abolished the Horse-Purchase Office's concurrent leadership;
translations.idiomatic: Now Shimin’s dual role as horse-purchase chief and tea chief blurred accountability; the court ended the combined appointment;

sentences.zh: 令茶場都大提舉視轉運使，同管幹視轉運判官，以重其任。

translations.literal: ordering the Tea Market Grand Supervisor to regard the transport commissioner, and joint managers to regard the transport vice commissioner—to weight their responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: elevating the tea grand supervisor to parity with the transport commissioner and joint managers to parity with the transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賈種民更立茶法，師閔論奏茶場與他場務不同，詔並用舊條。

translations.literal: Jia Zhongmin newly established a tea law; Shimin memorialized that tea markets differed from other market offices; an edict ordered use of the old articles together.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Zhongmin proposed a new tea law, Shimin argued tea markets differed from other agencies; the court kept the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 初，李杞增諸州茶場，自熙寧七年至元豐八年，蜀道茶場四十一，京西路金州為場六，陝西賣茶為場三百三十二，稅息至稷加為五十萬，及師閔為百萬。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Qi increased tea markets in the various prefectures; from Xining year 7 to Yuanfeng year 8, Shu route tea markets forty-one; Jingxi circuit Jin prefecture six markets; Shaanxi tea-selling markets three hundred thirty-two; tax interest reached fifty thousand under Ji’s increase, and under Shimin one million.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Qi’s expansion in Xining 7 through Yuanfeng 8 (1085), Sichuan had forty-one tea markets, Jingxi’s Jinzhou six, and Shaanxi three hundred thirty-two selling stations; annual tax profit rose from five hundred thousand under Ji to one million under Shimin.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，侍御史劉摯奏疏曰：“蜀茶之出，不過數十州，人賴以為生，茶司盡榷而市之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuan You, Attending Censor Liu Zhi submitted a memorial stating: "Shu tea's output does not exceed several tens of prefectures; people rely on it for livelihood—the Tea Office entirely monopolizes and markets it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan You 1 (1086) attending censor Liu Zhi memorialized: “Sichuan tea comes from only a few dozen prefectures on which people depend for livelihood, yet the Tea Office monopolizes and retails it all.

sentences.zh: 園戶有茶一本，而官市之，額至數十斤。

translations.literal: A plantation household has one tea [tree], yet the government buys it to a quota of several tens of jin.
translations.idiomatic: A grower with one bush may be forced to sell dozens of jin to the state.

sentences.zh: 官所給錢，靡耗於公者，名色不一，給借保任，輸入視驗，皆牙儈主之，故費於牙儈者又不知幾何。

translations.literal: Money the government gives is wasted in public charges under many nominal categories; advance loans require guarantors; delivery and inspection are all managed by brokers—therefore what is spent on brokers is again unknown how much.
translations.idiomatic: Official payment is eaten up by fees, guarantors, delivery, and inspection—all brokered—so broker charges alone are incalculable.

sentences.zh: 是官於園戶名為平市，而實奪之。

translations.literal: This is the government toward plantation households nominally fair-market, but in reality seizing from them.
translations.idiomatic: The state calls it fair purchase; in truth it seizes growers’ goods.

sentences.zh: 園戶有逃而免者，有投死以免者，而其害猶及鄰伍。

translations.literal: Plantation households have those who flee to escape, those who throw themselves to death to escape—and the harm still reaches neighboring households.
translations.idiomatic: Some flee, some die by suicide to escape—and neighbors still suffer.

sentences.zh: 欲伐茶則有禁，欲增植則加市，故其俗論謂地非生茶也，實生禍也。

translations.literal: Wishing to cut tea there is prohibition; wishing to plant more there is added purchase—therefore local custom says the land does not produce tea but truly produces calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting tea is forbidden; planting more triggers heavier purchase quotas—locals say the soil grows not tea but disaster.

sentences.zh: 願遣使者，考茶法之敝，以蘇蜀民。

translations.literal: We wish to dispatch envoys to examine the abuses of the tea law, to relieve Shu commoners.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that envoys review the tea law’s abuses and relieve the people of Shu.

sentences.zh: ”右司諫蘇轍繼言：“呂陶嚐奏改茶法，止行長引，令民自販，每緡長引錢百，詔從其請，民方有息肩之望。

translations.literal: " Right Office Remonstrator Su Zhe continued, saying: "Lü Tao once memorialized to change the tea law, implementing only long-distance transit permits, letting the people sell for themselves—one hundred cash per string for long-distance permits; an edict followed his request, and the people just then had hope of resting their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: ” Right Office remonstrator Su Zhe added: “Lü Tao once reformed the law to long-distance transit permits alone—growers could sell freely for one hundred cash per string. The throne approved and the people briefly hoped for relief.

sentences.zh: 孫迥、李稷入蜀商度，盡力掊取，息錢、長引並行，民間始不易矣。

translations.literal: Sun Jiong and Li Ji entered Shu to deliberate; they exhausted themselves in extraction; interest money and long-distance permits both operated—the people first were not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: But Sun Jiong and Li Ji went to Sichuan and imposed both profit tax and transit permits—the people were worse off than before.

sentences.zh: 且盜賊贓及二貫，止徒一年，出賞五千，今民有以錢八百私買茶四十斤者，輒徒一年，賞三十千，立法苟以自便，不顧輕重之宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, for stolen goods of two strings, penal servitude is only one year, with a reward of five thousand; now for a commoner who with eight hundred cash privately buys forty jin of tea, penal servitude of one year is immediately applied, reward thirty thousand—the law was made hastily for self-convenience, not considering fitness of severity and lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Theft of two strings brings one year’s penal servitude and a five-thousand reward; buying forty jin of tea privately for eight hundred cash brings one year and a thirty-thousand reward—laws drafted for official convenience without regard to proportion.

sentences.zh: 蓋造立茶法，皆傾險小人，不識事體。

translations.literal: In general, those who established the tea law were all unscrupulous petty men, not understanding the substance of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who framed the tea law were, in short, reckless petty officials who understood nothing of governance.

sentences.zh: ”且備陳五害。

translations.literal: " And in detail he set forth five harms.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then listed five specific harms.

sentences.zh: 呂陶亦條上利害，詔付黃廉體量；

translations.literal: Lü Tao also itemized advantages and harms; an edict referred it to Huang Lian for investigation;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Tao also submitted a detailed critique; the court ordered Huang Lian to investigate;

sentences.zh: 未至，摯又言陸師閔恣為不法，不宜仍任事。

translations.literal: before he arrived, Zhi again said Lu Shimin wantonly committed unlawful acts and should not be allowed to continue in office.
translations.idiomatic: before Huang arrived, Zhi again urged that Lu Shimin’s lawlessness disqualified him from office.

sentences.zh: 詔即罷之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promptly removed him.

sentences.zh: 先是，師閔提舉榷茶，所行職務，他司皆不得預聞，事權震灼，為患深密。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shimin supervised monopoly tea, the duties he executed—other offices all could not be informed in advance; his authority blazed hot, and the harm was deep and dense.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shimin the tea monopoly had operated in secrecy; other agencies could not intervene; his power was absolute and the abuses entrenched.

sentences.zh: 及黃廉就領茶事，乃請凡緣茶事有侵損戾法，或措置未當及有訴訟，依元豐令，聽他司關送。

translations.literal: When Huang Lian took charge of tea affairs, he then requested that whenever matters touching tea involved encroachment, violation of law, improper arrangement, or lawsuits, according to Yuanfeng regulations other offices might be notified to transmit [cases].
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Lian took over, he restored Yuanfeng rules allowing other offices to handle tea-related violations, disputes, and maladministration.

sentences.zh: 十一月，蒲宗孟亦以附會李稷賣茶罷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Pu Zongmeng was also dismissed for currying favor with Li Ji’s tea selling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Pu Zongmeng was dismissed for colluding in Li Ji’s tea monopoly.

sentences.zh: 明年，熙河、秦鳳、涇原三路茶仍官為計置，永興、鄜延、環慶許通商，凡以茶易穀者聽仍舊，毋得逾轉運司和糴價，其所博斛鬥勿取息。

translations.literal: The next year, Xi-He, Qin-Feng, and Jingyuan three circuits' tea was still planned by the government; Yongxing, Fuyan, and Huanqing permitted open trade; all who exchanged tea for grain were heard as before, not permitted to exceed the transport commissioner's harmonized grain-purchase price; grain exchanged for must not take interest.
translations.idiomatic: The following year government procurement continued on the Xi-He, Qin-Feng, and Jingyuan frontier, while Yongxing, Fuyan, and Huanqing allowed free trade; tea-for-grain exchanges followed old rules without exceeding the transport commissioner’s harmonized grain price, and no interest could be charged on grain received.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔成都等路茶事司，以三百萬緡為額本。

translations.literal: In year 7, an edict [set] the Chengdu and other circuits Tea Affairs Office with three million strings as quota capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 an edict fixed three million strings as capital quota for the Chengdu tea administration.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，復以陸師閔都大提舉成都等路茶事，而陝西復行禁榷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, Lu Shimin was again made Grand Supervisor of Chengdu and other circuits tea affairs, while Shaanxi again implemented prohibition monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 1 (1094) Lu Shimin was reappointed grand supervisor of Chengdu tea affairs, and Shaanxi’s monopoly was restored.

sentences.zh: 師閔乃奏龍州仍為禁茶地，凡茶法並用元豐舊條。

translations.literal: Shimin then memorialized that Long Prefecture should remain a forbidden-tea region, and that all tea regulations should uniformly use the old Yuanfeng articles.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin then memorialized that Long Prefecture should stay a restricted-tea zone and that every tea rule should revert to the Yuanfeng code.

sentences.zh: 師閔自復用，以訖哲宗之世，其掊克之跡，不若前日之著，故建明亦罕見焉。

translations.literal: From Shimin's restoration to office until the end of Emperor Zhezong's reign, the traces of his extortionate squeezing were not as conspicuous as in earlier days, so striking proposals were also rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: From his return to power through Zhezong's reign his extortion was less blatant than before, and bold new schemes were rare.

sentences.zh: 茶之在諸路者，神宗、哲宗朝無大更革。

translations.literal: As for tea in the various circuits, in the reigns of Emperor Shenzong and Emperor Zhezong there were no major changes.
translations.idiomatic: Tea policy in the regional circuits saw no major overhaul under Shenzong and Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 熙寧八年，嚐詔都提舉市易司歲賈商茶，以三百萬斤為額。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xining, an edict once ordered the Director-in-Chief of the Market Exchange Office annually to purchase merchant tea, with three million jin as the quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 8 (1075) the court ordered the Market Exchange Office to buy three million jin of merchant tea each year.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年，立六路茶稅租錢諸州通判轉運司月暨歲終比較都數之法。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou, regulations were established for the six circuits' tea-tax lease money: circuit intendants and transport commissioners were to compare monthly and year-end aggregate totals for all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 5 (1090) a system required the six tea circuits' intendants and transport commissioners to report and compare monthly and annual tea-tax totals for every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，以茶隸提刑司，稅務毋得更易為雜稅收受。

translations.literal: In year 7, tea was placed under the judicial-intendant offices, and tax stations were no longer permitted to change [collection] into miscellaneous taxes for receipt.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 tea enforcement was assigned to the judicial-intendant circuits, and tax stations could no longer substitute miscellaneous levies for tea dues.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，戶部言：“商旅茶稅五分，治平條立輸送之限既寬，復慮課入無準，故定以限約，毋得更展。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, the Ministry of Revenue said: "Traveling merchants' tea tax at five parts [in ten]—the Zhiping regulations set delivery deadlines that were already lenient; again fearing that revenue would lack a standard, therefore a fixed deadline was set, not to be extended further.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 4 (1097) the Ministry of Revenue reported: “The traveling-merchant tea tax at fifty percent: the Zhiping rules already allowed generous delivery deadlines; fearing unstable revenue, the court had fixed a firm deadline that must not be extended again.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，輒展以季，課入漏失。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou period, [officials] repeatedly extended [deadlines] by seasons, and revenue leaked away.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou officials kept extending deadlines by quarters, and collections fell short.

sentences.zh: 且茶稅歲計七十萬緡，積十年未嚐檢察，請內外委官，期一年驅算以聞。

translations.literal: Moreover, tea tax was reckoned at seven hundred thousand strings yearly; for ten years accumulated it had not been audited—[we] request appointing officials inside and outside [the capital], with a one-year deadline to drive through calculations and report.
translations.idiomatic: Tea tax was supposed to yield seven hundred thousand strings a year, yet no audit had been conducted in ten years; the ministry asked that officials be appointed inside and outside the capital to complete a full reckoning within one year and report back.

sentences.zh: ”詔聽其議，展限令出一時，毋承用。

translations.literal: " An edict approved their proposal; extension deadlines were to be issued as a one-time measure and not carried forward.
translations.idiomatic: ” The court approved the plan but ruled that any extension would be a one-time exception, not a standing policy.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，右仆射蔡京言：“祖宗立禁榷法，歲收淨利凡三百二十餘萬貫，而諸州商稅七十五萬貫有奇，食茶之算不在焉，其盛時幾五百餘萬緡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, Right Vice Director Cai Jing said: "The ancestors established the prohibition-monopoly law; annual net profit totaled more than 3.2 million guan, while the various prefectures' merchant tax was more than 750,000 guan—the reckoning for tea consumed was not included; at its height it was nearly more than five million strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 1 (1102) Right Vice Director Cai Jing said: “Our forebears’ monopoly law yielded more than 3.2 million guan in annual net profit, plus over 750,000 guan in prefectural merchant tax—not counting tea-consumption duties; at its peak revenue approached five million strings.

sentences.zh: 慶曆之後，法製浸壞，私販公行，遂罷禁榷，行通商之法。

translations.literal: After Qingli, the legal system gradually decayed; private trafficking went openly, and therefore prohibition monopoly was abolished, implementing the open-trade law.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qingli era the system eroded, smuggling flourished openly, and the monopoly was abandoned in favor of free trade.

sentences.zh: 自後商旅所至，與官為市，四十餘年，利源浸失。

translations.literal: From then on wherever traveling merchants went, they traded with the government; for more than forty years, sources of profit gradually drained away.
translations.idiomatic: For more than forty years merchants traded with the state wherever they went, and fiscal gains steadily drained away.

sentences.zh: 謂宜荊湖、江、淮、兩浙、福建七路所產茶，仍舊禁榷官買，勿復科民，即產茶州郡隨所置場，申商人園戶私易之禁，凡置場地園戶租折稅仍舊。

translations.literal: [He] said it was fitting that tea produced in the seven circuits Jing-Hu, Jiang, Huai, Liang-Zhe, and Fujian should still follow prohibition monopoly with official purchase, not again levying the people; at tea-producing prefectures and commanderies, according to established markets, report the ban on merchants' and plantation households' private dealings; wherever markets were established, plantation households' rent and converted tax should remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He urged restoring state purchase monopolies on tea from Jing-Hu, the Yangzi, Huai, Liang-Zhe, and Fujian—without levying the populace directly—reinstating market bans on private sales between merchants and growers, and leaving plantation rent and conversion taxes unchanged.

sentences.zh: 產茶州軍許其民赴場輸息，量限斤數，給短引，於旁近郡縣便鬻；

translations.literal: In tea-producing prefectures and armies, [the] people were permitted to go to markets to pay interest, with a measured limit on jin, and be given short permits, to sell conveniently in nearby prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: In producing districts growers could pay interest at the market up to a fixed weight limit, receive short permits, and sell nearby;

sentences.zh: 餘悉聽商人於榷貨務入納金銀、緡錢或並邊糧草，即本務給鈔，取便算請於場，別給長引，從所指州軍鬻之。

translations.literal: The remainder was entirely heard for merchants at the Monopoly Goods Office to pay in silver, gold, strings of cash, or frontier grain and fodder; the office then issued certificates, taking convenience to settle accounts at markets, separately issuing long permits, to sell according to the designated prefecture or army.
translations.idiomatic: all other tea would be sold by merchants who paid silver, cash, or frontier grain at the Monopoly Goods Office, received certificates, drew tea at the markets, and obtained long permits to sell in designated prefectures.

sentences.zh: 商稅自場給長引，沿道登時批發，至所指地，然後計稅盡輸，則在道無苛留。

translations.literal: Merchant tax from the market issuing long permits, along the route registering and issuing promptly, upon reaching the designated place, then calculating tax and paying in full—thus on the road there was no harsh detention.
translations.idiomatic: Tax would be stamped when the long permit was issued, recorded along the route, and paid in full only at the destination, so travelers were not detained and squeezed on the road.

sentences.zh: 買茶本錢以度牒、末鹽鈔、諸色封樁、坊場常平剩錢通三百萬緡為率，給諸路，諸路措置，各分命官。

translations.literal: Capital for buying tea used ordination certificates, residual salt certificates, various sealed-reserve funds, and surplus market and Ever-Normal Granary money, totaling three million strings as the rate, given to the various circuits; each circuit arranged matters and separately appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase capital of three million strings—drawn from ordination certificates, salt vouchers, sealed reserves, and market surplus funds—would be allocated to each circuit, with officials appointed locally to manage the scheme.

sentences.zh: ”詔悉聽焉。

translations.literal: " An edict approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: ” An edict approved the entire proposal.

sentences.zh: 俄定諸路措置茶事官置司：湖南於潭州，湖北於荊南，淮南於揚州，兩浙於蘇州，江東於江寧府，江西於洪州。

translations.literal: Soon regulations fixed tea-affairs arranging officials for each circuit and established offices: Hunan at Tan Prefecture, Hubei at Jingnan, Huainan at Yang Prefecture, Liang-Zhe at Su Prefecture, Jiangdong at Jiangning Prefecture, Jiangxi at Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were soon established for circuit tea commissioners: Hunan at Tanzhou, Hubei at Jingnan, Huainan at Yangzhou, Liang-Zhe at Suzhou, Jiangdong at Jiangning, and Jiangxi at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 其置場所在：蘄州即其州及蘄水縣，壽州以霍山、開順，光州以光山、固始，舒州即其州及羅源、太湖，黃州以麻城，廬州以舒城，常州以宜興，湖州即其州及長興、德清、安吉、武康，睦州即其州及青溪、分水、桐廬、遂安，婺州即其州及東陽、永康、浦江，處州即其州及遂昌、青田，蘇、杭、越各即其州，而越之上虞、餘姚、諸暨、新昌、剡縣皆置焉，衢、台各即其州，而溫州以平陽。

translations.literal: The places where markets were established: Qi Prefecture was that prefecture and Qishui County; Shou Prefecture used Huoshan and Kaishun; Guang Prefecture used Guangshan and Gushi; Shu Prefecture was that prefecture and Luoyuan and Taihu; Huang Prefecture used Macheng; Lu Prefecture used Shucheng; Chang Prefecture used Yixing; Hu Prefecture was that prefecture and Changxing, Deqing, Anji, and Wukang; Mu Prefecture was that prefecture and Qingxi, Fenshui, Tonglu, and Suian; Wu Prefecture was that prefecture and Dongyang, Yongkang, and Pujiang; Chu Prefecture was that prefecture and Suichang and Qingtian; Su, Hang, and Yue each used their prefecture, while in Yue, Shangyu, Yuyao, Zhuji, Xinchang, and Shan counties all had [markets]; Qu and Tai each used their prefecture, while Wen Prefecture used Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Markets were placed as follows: at Qizhou and Qishui; Huoshan and Kaishun in Shouzhou; Guangshan and Gushi in Guangzhou; Luoyuan and Taihu in Shuzhou; Macheng in Huangzhou; Shucheng in Luzhou; Yixing in Changzhou; Changxing, Deqing, Anji, and Wukang in Huzhou; Qingxi, Fenshui, Tonglu, and Suian in Muzhou; Dongyang, Yongkang, and Pujiang in Wuzhou; Suichang and Qingtian in Chuzhou; markets in Suzhou, Hangzhou, and Yuezhou, with additional sites in Shangyu, Yuyao, Zhuji, Xinchang, and Shan; Quzhou and Taizhou; and Pingyang in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 大法既定，其製置節目，不可毛舉。

translations.literal: Once the great law was fixed, its arrangement articles could not be enumerated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Once the main framework was set, its detailed provisions cannot be listed one by one.

sentences.zh: 四年，京復議更革，遂罷官置場，商旅並即所在州縣或京師給長短引，自買於園戶。

translations.literal: In year 4, Jing again discussed further reform, and therefore abolished official market establishment; traveling merchants together at their location's prefecture, county, or the capital were given long and short permits, buying themselves from plantation households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Jing pushed another overhaul: government markets were abolished, and merchants obtained long or short permits at local prefectures, counties, or the capital and bought directly from growers.

sentences.zh: 茶貯以籠篰，官為抽盤，循第敘輸息訖，批引販賣，茶事益加密矣。

translations.literal: Tea was stored in baskets and crates; the government conducted sampling inspections; in sequence by grade interest was paid and finished, permits were stamped for resale—the tea business grew ever more tightly controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Tea was stored in baskets and crates, inspected by officials, graded for interest payments, then stamped for resale—the trade grew ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，議提舉茶事司須保驗一路所產茶色高下、價直低昂，而請茶短引以地遠近程以三等之期。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, it was proposed that the Tea Affairs Supervision Office must guarantee and verify one circuit's produced tea quality high and low and price high and low, while for requesting tea short permits, according to distance near and far, deadlines were set in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 1 (1107) the tea supervision office was required to certify each circuit's tea grades and prices, and short-permit deadlines were set in three tiers by distance.

sentences.zh: 復慮商旅影挾舊引，冒詐規利，官吏因得擾動，以御筆申飭之。

translations.literal: Again fearing traveling merchants covertly carrying old permits, falsely scheming for profit, and officials thereby able to harass—an imperial brush-note admonished this.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing merchants would smuggle extra tea under old permits and that officials would exploit the fraud, the emperor issued a written admonition.

sentences.zh: 又以諸路再定茶息，多寡或不等，令後各增錢十。

translations.literal: Also, because the various circuits again fixed tea interest, more or less not equal, an order followed that each should add ten cash.
translations.idiomatic: Because circuits had reset tea interest at uneven rates, each circuit was ordered to add ten cash per unit.

sentences.zh: 三年，計七路一歲之息一百二十五萬一千九百餘緡，榷貨務再歲一百十有八萬五千餘緡。

translations.literal: In year 3, reckoning the seven circuits' one-year interest at 1,251,900-odd strings, the Monopoly Goods Office twice yearly 1,185,000-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the seven circuits yielded 1,251,900 strings in annual interest, and the Monopoly Goods Office another 1,185,000 strings over two years.

sentences.zh: 京專用是以舞智固權，自是歲以百萬緡輸京師所供私奉，掊息益厚，盜販公行，民滋病矣。

translations.literal: Jing exclusively used this to display cleverness and consolidate power; from then each year a million strings were sent to the capital for private stipends; squeezing interest grew thicker; smuggling went openly; the people grew ever more afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wielded these revenues to display cleverness and tighten his grip, sending a million strings yearly to the capital for private use; extortion deepened, smuggling flourished, and the people suffered more.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，大增損茶法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, the tea law was greatly increased and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 (1112) the tea law was overhauled again.

sentences.zh: 凡請長引再行者，輸錢百緡，即往陝西，加二十，茶以百二十斤；

translations.literal: All who requested long permits for a second journey paid one hundred strings; if going to Shaanxi, add twenty; tea was one hundred twenty jin;
translations.idiomatic: A second long permit cost one hundred strings; for Shaanxi add twenty, with tea fixed at one hundred twenty jin;

sentences.zh: 短引輸緡錢二十，茶以二十五斤。

translations.literal: Short permits paid twenty strings of cash; tea was twenty-five jin.
translations.idiomatic: short permits cost twenty strings for twenty-five jin of tea.

sentences.zh: 私造引者如川錢引法。

translations.literal: Those who privately manufactured permits were [punished] like the Sichuan money-permit law.
translations.idiomatic: Forging permits was punished under the same rules as Sichuan currency notes.

sentences.zh: 歲春茶出，集民戶約三歲實直及今價上戶部。

translations.literal: Each spring when tea came out, plantation households were assembled to estimate three years' true value and current price, reported upward to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring growers were assembled to fix three-year average and current prices for reporting to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 茶籠篰並皆官制，聽客買，定大小式，嚴封印之法。

translations.literal: Tea baskets and crates were all government-made; customers were permitted to buy; large and small patterns were fixed; sealing laws were strict.
translations.idiomatic: Official baskets and crates were standardized in size, sold to customers, and subject to strict sealing rules.

sentences.zh: 長短引輒竄改增減及新舊對帶、繳納申展、住賣轉鬻科條悉具。

translations.literal: Articles on tampering with long and short permits to increase or decrease, pairing old and new, payment and extension requests, halting sale and transferring resale—all were fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes covered tampering with permits, pairing old and new certificates, payment extensions, halting sales, and resale transfers in full detail.

sentences.zh: 初，客販茶用舊引者，未嚴斤重之限，影帶者眾。

translations.literal: At first, when traveling merchants sold tea using old permits, jin-weight limits were not strict; covert carriers were many.
translations.idiomatic: At first merchants using old permits faced no strict weight limits, and many smuggled extra tea.

sentences.zh: 於是又詔凡販長引斤重及三千斤者，須更買新引對賣，不及三千斤者，即用新引以一斤帶二斤鬻之，而合同場之法出矣。

translations.literal: Therefore an edict again [ordered]: all who sold on long permits with weight reaching three thousand jin must again buy new permits for paired sale; those not reaching three thousand jin used new permits to sell one jin carrying two jin—and the contract-market law emerged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required anyone selling three thousand jin on a long permit to buy a new paired permit; below that limit one jin on the new permit could carry two jin of tea—and the contract-market system was introduced.

sentences.zh: 場置於產茶州軍，而簿給於都茶場。

translations.literal: Markets were placed in tea-producing prefectures and armies, while registers and issuance were at the Capital Tea Market.
translations.idiomatic: Markets were located in producing prefectures, but ledgers and permits were issued at the capital tea office.

sentences.zh: 凡不限斤重茶委官司秤製，毋得止憑批引為定，有贏數即沒官，別定新引限程及重商旅規避秤製之禁，凡十八條，若避匿抄劄及擅賣，皆坐以徒。

translations.literal: All tea not limited by jin weight was entrusted to government offices for weighing; they must not rely only on stamped permits as fixed; surplus amounts were immediately confiscated by the state; separately new permit deadlines and heavy bans on traveling merchants evading weighing were fixed—eighteen articles in all; if concealing tally slips or unauthorized selling, all were sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: All tea had to be weighed by officials, not judged by permits alone; surplus was confiscated; eighteen articles set new permit deadlines and barred merchants from evading the scales; concealing tally slips or unauthorized sales brought penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 復慮茶法猶輕，課入不羨，定園戶私賣及有引而所賣逾數，保內有犯不告，並如煎鹽亭戶法。

translations.literal: Again fearing the tea law was still light and revenue not abundant, regulations fixed plantation households' private sales and those with permits who sold beyond quota, and mutual-responsibility groups with violations not reported—all like the boiled-salt boiler-household law.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the law was still too lenient and revenue too thin, private sales by growers, excess sales under permit, and neighbors who failed to report violations were punished like salt-boiler households.

sentences.zh: 短引及食茶關子輒出本路，坐以二千里流，賞錢百萬。

translations.literal: Short permits and tea-consumption tally slips taken out of the home circuit were sentenced to exile two thousand li; reward money one million.
translations.idiomatic: Taking short permits or tea ration slips outside the home circuit brought exile two thousand li and a reward of one million cash.

sentences.zh: 陝西舊通蜀茶，崇寧二年，始通東南茶。

translations.literal: Shaanxi formerly connected to Shu tea; in the second year of Chongning, it first connected to southeast tea.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi had long traded in Sichuan tea; in Chongning 2 (1103) southeastern tea was first admitted.

sentences.zh: 政和中，陝西沒官茶令估賣，繼以妨商旅，下令焚棄。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe period, Shaanxi confiscated official tea was ordered appraised and sold; subsequently because it hindered traveling merchants, an order was issued to burn and discard it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenghe confiscated tea in Shaanxi was ordered sold at appraisal; when that obstructed merchants, the court ordered it burned.

sentences.zh: 俄令正茶沒官者聽與販，引外剩茶及私茶數以給告者。

translations.literal: Soon an order [said] confiscated orthodox tea was permitted to be sold with [merchants]; surplus tea outside permits and private tea in number were given to informers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon confiscated licensed tea could be sold with merchants; surplus beyond permits and quantities of private tea were awarded to informers.

sentences.zh: 長引限以一年，短引限以半歲繳納。

translations.literal: Long permits were limited to one year; short permits limited to half a year for payment.
translations.idiomatic: Long permits expired in one year; short permits in six months.

sentences.zh: 久之，令已買引而未得於園戶者，期七年，許民間同見緡流轉，長引聽即本路住賣，以二浙鹽香司有言而止。

translations.literal: After a long time, an order [said] those who had bought permits but not yet obtained [tea] from plantation households had a seven-year deadline; private mutual witnessing of strings for circulation was permitted; long permits were heard to halt and sell within the home circuit—stopped because the Liang-Zhe Salt and Incense Office spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Later holders who had bought permits but not yet drawn tea from growers were given seven years; private transfer of permits was allowed, and long permits could be held for local resale until the Liang-Zhe Salt and Incense Office objected and the rule was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 其科條纖悉紛更，不可勝記，慮商旅疑豫，茶貨不通，乃重扇搖之令。

translations.literal: Its articles were minute and changed repeatedly, too many to record; fearing traveling merchants would hesitate and tea goods would not circulate, fan-waving orders were again issued.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions multiplied and shifted beyond counting; fearing merchants would hesitate and trade would stall, the court again issued reassuring edicts.

sentences.zh: 於時掊克之吏，爭以贏羨為功，朝廷亦嚴立比較之法。

translations.literal: At that time extortionate officials competed to take surplus as achievement; the court also strictly established comparison regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Extortionate officials competed to report surpluses as merit, and the court imposed strict performance comparisons.

sentences.zh: 州郡樂賞畏刑，惟恐負課，優假商人，陵轢州郡，蓋莫有言者。

translations.literal: Prefectures and commanderies delighted in rewards and feared punishment, only afraid of falling short on revenue; they indulged merchants and bullied prefectures and commanderies—there was essentially no one who spoke out.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, eager for rewards and fearful of punishment, coddled merchants and bullied their own districts to meet quotas—and almost no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 獨邠州通判張益謙奏：“陝西非產茶地，奉行十年，未經立額，歲歲比較，第務增益，稍或虧少，程督如星。

translations.literal: Only Bin Prefecture Vice Prefect Zhang Yiqian memorialized: "Shaanxi is not a tea-producing region; [the law] has been enforced ten years without establishing a quota; year after year comparisons [are made], only striving to increase; if slightly deficient, supervision presses like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Yiqian, vice prefect of Binzhou, memorialized: “Shaanxi does not produce tea, yet the law has been enforced for ten years without a fixed quota; yearly comparisons demand ever higher yields, and the slightest shortfall brings relentless pressure.

sentences.zh: 州縣懼殿，多前路招誘豪商，增價以幸其來，故陝西茶價，斤有至五六緡者，或稍裁之，則批改文引，轉之他郡。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties feared dismissal; many went ahead to entice powerful merchants, raising prices to hope for their coming—thus Shaanxi tea prices per jin reached five or six strings; if slightly cut, then permits were altered in writing and transferred to other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing dismissal, prefectures enticed wealthy merchants with inflated prices, so tea in Shaanxi reached five or six strings per jin; if prices were trimmed, permits were altered and the tea routed to other counties.

sentences.zh: 及配之鋪戶，安能盡售？

translations.literal: When allocated to shop households, how could they sell it all?
translations.idiomatic: When tea was forced on retail shops, how could they sell it all?

sentences.zh: 均及稅農，民實受害，徒令豪商坐享大利。

translations.literal: Spread to tax-paying farmers, the people truly suffered harm; it only let powerful merchants sit and enjoy great profit.
translations.idiomatic: The burden was spread to tax-paying farmers who truly suffered, while wealthy merchants reaped the profit.

sentences.zh: ”言竟不行。

translations.literal: " In the end the memorial was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: ” His protest was ignored.

sentences.zh: 然自茶法更張，至政和六年，收息一千萬緡，茶增一千二百八十一萬五十一百餘斤。

translations.literal: Yet from the tea law's overhaul until the sixth year of Zhenghe, interest collected was ten million strings; tea increased by 12,815,100-odd jin.
translations.idiomatic: From the overhaul through Zhenghe 6 (1116), however, interest reached ten million strings and tea volume rose by more than 12.81 million jin.

sentences.zh: 及方臘竊發，乃詔權罷比較。

translations.literal: When Fang La's rebellion broke out, an edict temporarily suspended comparisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La's rebellion erupted, the court temporarily suspended performance comparisons.

sentences.zh: 臘誅，有司議招集園戶，借貸優恤，止於文具，奸臣仍用事，蠹國害民，又慮人言，扇搖之令復出矣。

translations.literal: After La was executed, responsible offices discussed gathering plantation households, lending and preferential relief—only on paper; treacherous ministers still held power, harming the state and injuring the people; again fearing public talk, fan-waving orders reappeared.
translations.idiomatic: After Fang La was killed, officials debated relief loans for growers, but it remained paperwork; corrupt ministers still ruled, draining the state and harming the people, and reassuring edicts were issued again for fear of public criticism.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔川茶侵客茶地者，以多寡差定其罪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict [said] those whose Sichuan tea encroached on guest-tea regions should have crimes differentiated by more or less.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 (1126) an edict fixed penalties for Sichuan tea encroaching on other regions according to the amount involved.

sentences.zh: 初，熙寧五年，以福建茶陳積，乃詔福建茶在京、京東西、淮南、陝西、河東仍禁榷，餘路通商。

translations.literal: At first, in the fifth year of Xining, because Fujian tea piled up stale, an edict [said] Fujian tea in the capital, Jingdong East and West, Huainan, Shaanxi, and Hedong still followed prohibition monopoly; remaining circuits had open trade.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in Xining 5 (1072), stale Fujian tea stockpiles led the court to keep Fujian tea under monopoly in the capital, Jingdong, Huainan, Shaanxi, and Hedong while allowing free trade elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 元豐七年，王子京為福建轉運副使，言“建州臘茶，舊立榷法，自熙寧權聽通商，自此茶戶售客人茶甚良，官中所得惟常茶，稅錢極微，南方遺利，無過於此，乞仍舊行榷法。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng, Wang Zijing as Fujian Transport Vice Commissioner said: "Jian Prefecture tribute tea—formerly a monopoly law was established; since Xining it was temporarily heard for open trade; from then tea households sold guests' tea of very fine quality, while what the government obtained was only ordinary tea; tax money was extremely slight—southern lost profit, nothing exceeded this—[we] beg to restore the former monopoly law.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 7 (1084) Wang Zijing, Fujian transport vice commissioner, argued: “Jianzhou tribute tea was once monopolized; since Xining free trade has let growers sell their best tea to merchants while the state receives only ordinary grades for a pittance—no greater loss in the south; we ask that the monopoly be restored.

sentences.zh: 建州歲出茶不下三百萬斤，南劍州亦不下二十餘萬斤，欲盡買入官，度逐州軍民戶多少及約鄰路民用之數計置，即官場賣，嚴立告賞禁。

translations.literal: Jian Prefecture yearly output of tea was not less than three million jin; Nanjian Prefecture also not less than two hundred thousand-odd jin—[we] wish entirely to buy into government [stores], estimating each prefecture and army's civilian households more or less and approximating neighboring circuits' civilian use to plan arrangement, then selling at government markets, strictly establishing informer rewards and bans.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou produces at least three million jin yearly and Nanjian over two hundred thousand; we propose buying it all for government sale after estimating local population and neighboring demand, with strict informer rewards and prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 建州賣私末茶，借豐國監錢十萬緡為本。

translations.literal: Jian Prefecture selling private powdered tea borrowed one hundred thousand strings from Fengguo Directorate funds as capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou's sale of private powdered tea would be capitalized with one hundred thousand strings borrowed from the Fengguo Directorate.

sentences.zh: ”並從之；

translations.literal: " All was approved;
translations.idiomatic: ” The court approved all of it;

sentences.zh: 所請均入諸路榷賣，委轉運司官提舉：福建王子京，兩浙許懋，江東杜偉，江西朱彥博，廣東高鎛，然子京蓋未免抑配於民。

translations.literal: What was requested was evenly entered into various circuits' monopoly sale; transport-commissioner officials were entrusted to supervise: Fujian Wang Zijing, Liang-Zhe Xu Mao, Jiangdong Du Wei, Jiangxi Zhu Yanbo, Guangdong Gao Bang—but Zijing probably still could not avoid forced allocation on the people.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved for monopoly sales across circuits under transport commissioners: Wang Zijing in Fujian, Xu Mao in Liang-Zhe, Du Wei in Jiangdong, Zhu Yanbo in Jiangxi, and Gao Bang in Guangdong—though Zijing still imposed forced quotas on the people.

sentences.zh: 時遠方若桂州修仁諸縣、夔州路達州有司皆議榷茶，言利者踵相躡，然神宗聞鄂州失催茶稅，輒蠲之。

translations.literal: At that time distant regions such as Guizhou Xiuren and other counties, Kuizhou circuit Dazhou—officials all discussed monopoly tea; those speaking of profit followed one after another; yet when Emperor Shenzong heard E Prefecture had lost urged tea tax, he immediately remitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Distant districts such as Xiuren in Guizhou and Dazhou in Kuizhou also debated tea monopolies as profit-seekers piled on, yet when Shenzong learned that Ezhou had failed to collect tea tax, he promptly remitted it.

sentences.zh: 建州園戶等以茶粗濫當剝納，為錢三萬六千餘緡，慮其不能償，令準輸茶。

translations.literal: Jian Prefecture plantation households and others, because tea was coarse and inferior, were to be stripped and levied, amounting to more than thirty-six thousand strings—fearing they could not repay, an order allowed payment in tea.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou growers faced a levy of more than thirty-six thousand strings for inferior tea they could not pay in cash, so the court allowed payment in tea instead.

sentences.zh: 初，成都帥司蔡延慶言邛部川蠻主苴克等願賣馬，即詔延慶以茶招來，後聞邊計蠻情非便，即罷之。

translations.literal: At first, Chengdu commandery commissioner Cai Yanqing said Qiong-Bu-Chuan barbarian chief Juke and others wished to sell horses; an edict then ordered Yanqing to recruit them with tea; later hearing frontier planning that barbarian sentiment was not suitable, it was immediately abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Chengdu commissioner Cai Yanqing reported that Qiong-Bu-Chuan chief Juke wished to sell horses, and the court ordered tea used to attract them; when frontier officials judged the policy unwise, it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 哲宗嗣位，御史安惇首劾王子京買臘茶抑民，詔罷子京事任，令福建禁榷州軍視其舊，餘並通商。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong succeeded, Censor An Dun first impeached Wang Zijing for buying tribute tea and oppressing the people; an edict dismissed Zijing from his duties, ordering Fujian monopoly prefectures and armies to regard their former [status], the rest all open trade.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong succeeded, Censor An Dun impeached Wang Zijing for buying tribute tea and oppressing the people; Zijing was removed, Fujian monopoly districts reverted to prior rules, and the rest returned to free trade.

sentences.zh: 桂州修仁等縣禁榷及陝西碎賣芽茶皆罷。

translations.literal: Guizhou Xiuren and other counties' prohibition monopoly and Shaanxi's fragmented sale of bud tea were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Monopolies in Xiuren and other Guizhou counties and Shaanxi's retail sale of bud tea were abolished.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，尚書有言：“建、劍二州茶額七十餘萬斤，近歲增盛，而本錢多不繼。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning, the Secretariat said: "Jian and Jian two prefectures' tea quota more than seven hundred thousand jin; in recent years it increased and flourished, while capital often could not continue.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 2 the Secretariat reported: “Jian and Nanjian produce over seven hundred thousand jin yearly, output has grown, but purchase capital often runs short.

sentences.zh: ”詔更給度牒四百，仍給以諸色封樁。

translations.literal: " An edict further granted four hundred ordination certificates and still supplied various sealed-reserve funds.
translations.idiomatic: ” The court issued four hundred more ordination certificates and additional sealed-reserve funds.

sentences.zh: 繼詔商旅販臘茶蠲其稅，私販者治元售之家，如元豐之製。

translations.literal: Subsequently an edict [said] traveling merchants selling tribute tea were exempted from its tax; private traffickers were punished at the original selling household, like the Yuanfeng system.
translations.idiomatic: A follow-up edict exempted merchants' tribute-tea sales from tax and punished private trafficking at the source household, as under Yuanfeng rules.

sentences.zh: 臘茶舊法免稅，大觀三年，措置茶事，始收焉。

translations.literal: Tribute tea under the old law was tax-exempt; in the third year of Daguan, arranging tea affairs, collection began.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute tea had been tax-exempt; in Daguan 3 (1109) the tea administration began collecting tax on it.

sentences.zh: 四年，私販勿治元售之家，如元符令。

translations.literal: In year 4, private trafficking was not to punish the original selling household, like the Yuanfu order.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 private trafficking no longer punished the source household, per Yuanfu rules.

sentences.zh: 政和初，復增損為新法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenghe, it was again increased and reduced into a new law.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenghe the law was revised again.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔免輸短引，許依長引於諸路住賣，後末骨茶每長引增五百斤，短引仿此；

translations.literal: In year 3, an edict exempted paying for short permits, permitting according to long permits to halt and sell in various circuits; later powdered tea for each long permit added five hundred jin, short permits imitated this;
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 an edict waived short-permit fees and allowed sales under long permits across circuits; later powdered tea added five hundred jin per long permit, with short permits following suit;

sentences.zh: 諸路監司、州郡公使食茶禁私買，聽依商旅買引。

translations.literal: Various circuits' surveillance commissioners and prefectural envoys' tea for consumption banned private purchase; they were heard to follow traveling merchants in buying permits.
translations.idiomatic: circuit commissioners and prefectural envoys were barred from private tea purchases and had to buy permits like merchants.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔福建茶園如鹽田，量土地產茶多寡，依等第均稅。

translations.literal: In year 6, an edict [said] Fujian tea gardens like salt fields: measuring land's tea output more or less, according to grades evenly taxing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Fujian tea gardens were taxed like salt fields, with rates set by graded land productivity.

sentences.zh: 重和元年，以改給免稅新引，重定福建末茶斤重，長引以六百斤為率。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chonghe, because of changing issuance of tax-exempt new permits, Fujian powdered tea jin weight was refixed; long permits took six hundred jin as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: In Chonghe 1 (1118) new tax-exempt permits were issued and Fujian powdered-tea weights were reset, with long permits fixed at six hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，宋用臣都提舉汴河堤岸，創奏修置水磨。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng period, Song Yongchen as Director-in-Chief of Bian River Embankments memorialized to create and establish water mills.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfeng Song Yongchen, director of Bian River embankments, proposed building water-powered tea mills.

sentences.zh: 凡在京茶戶擅磨末茶者有禁，並許赴官請買。

translations.literal: All capital tea households who on their own ground powdered tea had a ban, and were also permitted to go to government to request purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Capital tea dealers were forbidden to grind powdered tea privately but could apply to buy from the government mills.

sentences.zh: 而茶鋪入米豆雜物揉和者募人告，一兩賞三千，及一斤十千，至五十千止。

translations.literal: As for tea shops mixing in rice, beans, and miscellaneous adulterants—recruiting people to inform: one liang rewarded three thousand, up to one jin ten thousand, to fifty thousand at most.
translations.idiomatic: Tea shops adulterating tea with grain or beans faced informer rewards of three thousand cash per liang detected, ten thousand per jin, up to fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 商賈販茶應往府界及在京師，須令產茶山場州軍給引，並赴京場中賣，犯者依私販臘茶法。

translations.literal: Merchants selling tea who should go to the metropolitan circuit and the capital had to have producing-region mountain markets and prefectures and armies issue permits, and all go to capital markets to sell; violators followed the private trafficking tribute-tea law.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants selling tea in the metropolitan circuit or capital had to obtain permits from producing districts and sell at capital markets; violators were punished like illegal tribute-tea traffickers.

sentences.zh: 諸路末茶入府界者，復嚴為之禁。

translations.literal: Powdered tea from various circuits entering the metropolitan circuit again had strict bans imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Powdered tea from other circuits entering the metropolitan region was again strictly banned.

sentences.zh: 訖元豐末，歲獲息不過二十萬，商旅病焉。

translations.literal: By the end of Yuanfeng, yearly profit obtained was not more than two hundred thousand; traveling merchants were afflicted by it.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Yuanfeng annual profit barely reached two hundred thousand strings, and merchants suffered under the system.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，寬茶法，議者欲罷水磨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, the tea law was relaxed; discussants wished to abolish water mills.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou the tea law was relaxed and some officials proposed abolishing the water mills.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎李定以失歲課，持不可廢；

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue Vice Minister Li Ding, because yearly revenue would be lost, maintained they could not be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Li Ding argued they could not be abolished without losing annual revenue;

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉摯、右司諫蘇轍等相繼論奏，遂罷。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Liu Zhi, Right Bureau Remonstrator Su Zhe, and others in succession memorialized; [the mills] were then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Liu Zhi, Remonstrator Su Zhe, and others memorialized in turn, and the mills were abolished.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，章惇等用事，首議修復水磨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Zhang Dun and others held power; they first discussed restoring water mills.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng, with Zhang Dun in power, officials first moved to restore the water mills.

sentences.zh: 乃詔即京、索、大源等河為之，以孫迥提舉，復命兼提舉汴河堤岸。

translations.literal: An edict then [ordered] establishing them on the Jing, Suo, Dayuan, and other rivers; Sun Jiong was made supervisor, again ordered concurrently to supervise Bian River embankments.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts placed mills on the Jing, Suo, Dayuan, and other rivers under Sun Jiong, who was also reappointed to oversee Bian River embankments.

sentences.zh: 四年，場官錢景逢獲息十六萬餘緡，呂安中二十一萬餘緡，以差議賞。

translations.literal: In year 4, market official Qian Jingfeng obtained profit of more than one hundred sixty thousand strings; Lü Anzhong more than two hundred ten thousand strings—rewards were deliberated by rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 market officer Qian Jingfeng reported profit of more than 160,000 strings and Lü Anzhong more than 210,000; rewards were set by rank.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，戶部上凡獲私末茶並雜和者，即犯者未獲，估價給賞，並如私臘茶獲犯人法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, the Ministry of Revenue reported: all who seized private powdered tea and adulterated mixtures—even if the violator was not seized—appraised value was given as reward, all like the law for seizing private tribute-tea violators.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1 (1098) the Ministry of Revenue ruled that seized private powdered or adulterated tea merited appraisal rewards even if the offender escaped, under the same rules as illegal tribute-tea cases.

sentences.zh: 雜和茶宜棄者，斤特給二十錢，至十緡止。

translations.literal: Adulterated tea fit to be discarded: per jin specially given twenty cash, up to ten strings at most.
translations.idiomatic: For adulterated tea to be destroyed, informers received twenty cash per jin detected, up to ten strings.

sentences.zh: 初，元豐中修置水磨，止於在京及開封府界諸縣，未始行於外路。

translations.literal: At first, Yuanfeng's establishment of water mills was only in the capital and Kaifeng metropolitan circuit counties; it had not been implemented in outer circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Yuanfeng mills were built only in the capital and Kaifeng metropolitan counties, not in outer circuits.

sentences.zh: 及紹聖復置，其後遂於京西鄭、滑、潁昌府，河北澶州皆行之，又將即濟州山口營置。

translations.literal: When Shaosheng restored them, afterward they were implemented in Jingxi Zheng, Hua, and Yingchang prefectures, Hebei Cao Prefecture—all; also planned to establish at Jizhou Shankou camp.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaosheng restoration they spread to Zhengzhou, Huazhou, and Yingchang in Jingxi and Cao Prefecture in Hebei, with plans for a site at Jizhou Shankou.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，提舉京城茶場所奏：“紹聖初，興復水磨，歲收二十六萬餘緡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning, the Capital Tea Market Supervisor memorialized: "At the beginning of Shaosheng, restoring water mills, yearly collection was more than two hundred sixty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 2 the capital tea-market supervisor reported: “When Shaosheng restored the mills, annual revenue exceeded 260,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 四年，於長葛等處京、索、潩水河增修磨二百六十餘所，自輔郡榷法罷，遂失其利，請復舉行。

translations.literal: In year 4, at Changge and other places on the Jing, Suo, and Weishui rivers, more than two hundred sixty mills were added and repaired; since the auxiliary commandery monopoly law was abolished, profit was then lost—[we] request restoration and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 more than 260 mills were added along the Jing, Suo, and Weishui rivers near Changge; when the auxiliary-commandery monopoly ended, profits vanished—we ask that the mills be restored.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 尋詔商販臘茶入京城者，本場盡買之，其翻引出外者，收堆垛錢。

translations.literal: Soon an edict [said] merchants selling tribute tea entering the capital—the market entirely bought it; those who turned permits to take it outside paid stacking-storage money.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict required the capital market to buy all tribute tea brought in by merchants and charged storage fees for tea taken back out under permit.

sentences.zh: 裁元豐製更立新額，歲買山場草茶以五百萬斤為率。

translations.literal: [They] cut the Yuanfeng regulations and established new quotas; yearly purchase of mountain-field rough tea took five million jin as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng rules were trimmed and new quotas set, with annual purchases of mountain-field rough tea fixed at five million jin.

sentences.zh: 客茶至京者，許官場買十之三，即索價故高，驗元引買價量增。

translations.literal: For guest merchants' tea arriving at the capital, [they] permitted the government market to buy three-tenths; [merchants] then demanded prices therefore high, and verifying Yuanfeng permit purchase prices, quantities were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants bringing tea to the capital had to sell three-tenths to the government depot, which drove up prices; purchase amounts on Yuanfeng permits were raised accordingly.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔罷之。

translations.literal: In year 3, an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 an edict abolished the measure.

sentences.zh: 明年，改令磨戶承歲課視酒戶納曲錢法。

translations.literal: The next year, [they] changed orders so mill households bore the annual levy, following the wine-household yeast-money payment law.
translations.idiomatic: The next year mill households were made to bear the annual levy on the model of distillers paying yeast-money dues.

sentences.zh: 五年，復罷民戶磨茶，官用水磨仍依元豐法，應緣茶事並隸都提舉汴河堤岸司。

translations.literal: In year 5, [they] again abolished common households grinding tea; government water mills still followed Yuanfeng law; all matters connected with tea were placed under the Metropolitan Bian River Embankment Supervisory Office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 private milling was abolished again; official water mills followed Yuanfeng rules, and all tea affairs were placed under the metropolitan Bian River embankment office.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，改以提舉茶事司為名，尋命茶場、茶事通為一司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, [the office] was renamed the Tea Affairs Supervisory Office; soon tea markets and tea affairs were ordered unified as one office.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 1 (1107) it was renamed the Tea Affairs Supervisory Office, and soon tea markets and tea administration were merged into one agency.

sentences.zh: 三年，復撥隸京城所，一用舊法。

translations.literal: In year 3, [it] was again reassigned to the Capital Markets Office; old methods alone were used.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 authority reverted to the Capital Markets Office and former practice was restored in full.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，京城所請商旅販茶起引定入京住賣者，即許借江入汴，如元豐舊制；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, the Capital Markets Office requested: for traveling merchants selling tea who obtained permits fixed for entry to the capital to reside and sell, then permit borrowing the Yangtze channel to enter the Bian, as Yuanfeng old regulations;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 1 (1111) the Capital Markets Office asked that merchants who took out permits to bring tea into the capital for local sale be allowed, as under Yuanfeng, to use the Yangtze route into the Bian;

sentences.zh: 其借江入汴卻指他路住賣者禁，已請引者並令赴京。

translations.literal: those who borrowed the Yangtze to enter the Bian yet designated other circuits for residing and selling were forbidden; those who had already obtained permits were all ordered to proceed to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: but those who used that route yet planned to sell in other circuits were forbidden, and holders of existing permits were ordered to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年，以課入不登，商賈留滯，詔以其事歸尚書省。

translations.literal: In year 2, because levy receipts did not meet targets and merchants were detained in place, an edict ordered the matter returned to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, with revenues falling short and merchants stuck in transit, an edict returned tea administration to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書省言：“水磨茶自元豐創立，止行於近畿，昨乃分配諸路，以故至弊，欲止行於京城，仍行通客販，餘路水磨並罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Revenue said: "Water-mill tea since Yuanfeng's founding operated only in the near capital region; recently it was distributed to all circuits, and for this reason reached extreme abuse—we wish to limit operation to the capital, still permit general merchant sales, and abolish water mills in the remaining circuits altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry then reported: “Water-mill tea, introduced in Yuanfeng, had worked only in the capital region; spreading it to every circuit caused the worst abuses. We propose limiting mills to the capital, keeping open trade to merchants, and abolishing mills elsewhere.”

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，收息四百萬貫有奇，比舊三倍，遂創月進。

translations.literal: In year 4, collected interest exceeded four million strings, three times the old amount; monthly tribute deliveries were then instituted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 profits exceeded four million strings—triple the former take—and monthly deliveries to court were instituted.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎初，於真州印鈔，給賣東南茶鹽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan under Gaozong, at Zhen Prefecture notes were printed to supply sale of Southeast tea and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan, Gaozong's court printed notes at Zhen Prefecture to fund sales of southeastern tea and salt.

sentences.zh: 當是時，茶之產於東南者，浙東西、江東西、湖南北、福建、淮南、廣東西，路十，州六十有六，縣二百四十有二。

translations.literal: At that time, for tea produced in the Southeast: Zhe East and West, Jiang East and West, Hunan North and South, Fujian, Huainan, and Guang East and West—ten circuits, sixty-six prefectures, two hundred forty-two counties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time southeastern tea came from ten circuits—eastern and western Zhe, Jiang, Hunan, Fujian, Huainan, and Guang—spanning sixty-six prefectures and 242 counties.

sentences.zh: 霅川顧渚生石上者謂之紫筍，毗陵之陽羨，紹興之日鑄，婺源之謝源，隆興之黃龍、雙井，皆絕品也。

translations.literal: At Guzhu in Zha Prefecture, what grows on stone is called Purple Shoot; Yangxian of Piling, Rizhu of Shaoxing, Xieyuan of Wuyuan, Huanglong and Shuangjing of Longxing—all were supreme grades.
translations.idiomatic: Famed grades included Purple Shoot from stone-grown Guzhu tea in Zha, Yangxian from Piling, Rizhu from Shaoxing, Xieyuan from Wuyuan, and Huanglong and Shuangjing from Longxing.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，置行在都茶場，罷合同場十有八，惟洪、江、興國、潭、建各置場一，監官一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, the traveling-court metropolitan tea market was established; eighteen joint-contract depots were abolished—only Hong, Jiang, Xingguo, Tan, and Jian each had one market set up, one supervising official each.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 the court set up a metropolitan tea market at the temporary capital, closed eighteen joint-contract depots, and retained one market and one supervisor each at Hong, Jiang, Xingguo, Tan, and Jian.

sentences.zh: 罷食茶小引，捕私茶法視捕私鹽。

translations.literal: Small permits for personal-consumption tea were abolished; the law for seizing private tea was treated like seizing private salt.
translations.idiomatic: Small permits for household tea were abolished, and penalties for illegal tea matched those for illegal salt.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，秦檜等始進《茶鹽法》。

translations.literal: In year 21, Qin Hui and others first presented the Tea and Salt Law.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 Qin Hui and others first submitted the Tea and Salt Code.

sentences.zh: 先是，臣僚或因事建明，朝廷亦因時損益，至是審訂成書，上之。

translations.literal: Earlier, officials had proposed measures on particular occasions; the court also adjusted gains and losses according to the times—now these were examined, fixed into a book, and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had long proposed piecemeal reforms and the court had adjusted policy as needed; now the rules were reviewed, codified, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興二年，淮東宣諭錢端禮言：“商販長引茶，水路不許過高郵，陸路不許過天長。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing under Xiaozong, Huaidong Commissioner Qian Duanli said: "For merchants' long permits for tea, by water route [they] were not permitted to pass Gaoyou; by land route [they] were not permitted to pass Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 2 (1164) Huaidong commissioner Qian Duanli proposed: “Tea on long permits may not pass Gaoyou by water or Tianchang by land.

sentences.zh: 如願往楚州及盱眙界，引貼輸翻引錢十貫五百文；

translations.literal: If [they] wished to go to Chuzhou and the Xuyi border, [they] affixed permits and paid supplemental permit money of ten strings five hundred cash;
translations.idiomatic: Merchants bound for Chuzhou or the Xuyi frontier must pay a supplemental permit fee of ten strings and five hundred cash;

sentences.zh: 如又過淮北，貼輸亦如之。

translations.literal: if [they] again crossed north of the Huai, affixed payment was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: and the same fee applies for crossing north of the Huai.”

sentences.zh: ”當是時，商販自榷場轉入虜中，其利至博，幾禁雖嚴，而民之犯法者自若也。

translations.literal: " At that time, merchants from monopoly exchange markets turned [tea] into the barbarian lands; the profit was extremely broad—though prohibitions were strict, common people who violated the law were as before.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yet merchants still funneled tea from monopoly markets into Jurchen territory for vast profit, and despite strict bans illegal trade continued unchecked.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，戶部言：“商販至淮北榷場折博，除輸翻引錢，更輸通貨儈息錢十一緡五百文。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao, the Ministry of Revenue said: "Merchants reaching north-of-Huai monopoly exchange markets for barter exchange, besides paying supplemental permit money, further paid general-trade brokerage-interest money of eleven strings five hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 2 (1166) the Ministry of Revenue ruled that merchants bartering at north-of-Huai monopoly markets must pay, beyond supplemental permit fees, a brokerage charge of eleven strings and five hundred cash.

sentences.zh: ”八年，減輸翻引錢止七緡，通貨儈見錢止八緡。

translations.literal: " In year 8, supplemental permit money paid was reduced to only seven strings; general-trade brokerage cash-in-hand was only eight strings.
translations.idiomatic: ” In year 8 supplemental permit fees were cut to seven strings and the brokerage charge to eight strings cash.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，以長短茶引權以半依原引斤重錢數，分作四緡小引印給，而翻引貼輸錢隨小引輸送。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, long and short tea permits were temporarily halved according to original permit jin-weight and money amounts, divided and issued as four-string small permits, while supplemental permit affixed payments followed small-permit submission.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 (1175) long and short tea permits were temporarily split in half by weight and fee, reissued as four-string small permits, with supplemental fees paid on the small-permit basis.

sentences.zh: 光宗紹熙初，漳州守臣朱熹奏除屬邑科茶七千餘緡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxi under Guangzong, Zhangzhou defending official Zhu Xi memorialized to remove tea levies on subordinate counties of more than seven thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxi, Zhangzhou prefect Zhu Xi memorialized to abolish tea levies totaling more than seven thousand strings in subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 臣僚申明長短小引相兼，從人之便。

translations.literal: Officials clarified that long and short small permits could be used together, following people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Officials ruled that long and short small permits could be used together for merchants' convenience.

sentences.zh: 戶部言給賣小引，除金銀、會子分數入輸，餘願專以會子算請者聽。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue said that in issuing small permits for sale, besides gold, silver, and huizi paid in fractional portions, for the remainder those who wished to calculate requests solely in huizi were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry allowed small permits to be bought partly in gold, silver, or huizi paper notes, with the balance payable entirely in huizi if the merchant chose.

sentences.zh: 寧宗嘉泰四年，知隆興府韓邈奏請：“隆興府惟分寧縣產茶，他縣無茶，而豪民武斷者乃請引，窮索一鄉，使認茶租，非便。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiatai under Ningzong, Longxing prefecture intendant Han Miao memorialized: "In Longxing Prefecture only Fenning County produces tea; other counties have no tea, yet powerful men who monopolized by force obtained permits, exhaustively searching one township to make [people] acknowledge tea rent—this is not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiatai 4 (1204) Longxing prefect Han Miao reported: “Only Fenning County in Longxing produces tea, yet local strongmen obtain permits and squeeze whole townships for tea rents where no tea grows.

sentences.zh: ”於是禁非產茶縣不許民擅認茶租。

translations.literal: " Thereupon [they] forbade counties that did not produce tea from allowing common people to claim tea rent on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: ” The court then barred counties without tea production from allowing private claims to tea rent.

sentences.zh: 建寧臘茶，北苑為第一，其最佳者曰社前，次曰火前，又曰雨前，所以供玉食，備賜予。

translations.literal: Jianning tribute tea—Beiyuan was first; its finest was called Before the Sacrifice, next Before the Fire, again Before the Rain—these supplied imperial food and prepared bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jianning tribute teas Beiyuan ranked first; its finest grades were Before the Sacrifice, then Before the Fire, then Before the Rain, reserved for the imperial table and court gifts.

sentences.zh: 太平興國始置，大觀以後製愈精，數愈多，胯式屢變，而品不一，歲貢片茶二十一萬六千斤。

translations.literal: It was first established in Taiping Xingguo; after Daguan craftsmanship grew ever finer, quantities ever greater, cake molds repeatedly changed, yet grades were not uniform—yearly tribute of cake tea was two hundred sixteen thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: The garden was founded in Taiping Xingguo; after Daguan craftsmanship grew finer, output larger, and cake molds ever-changing, with grades proliferating, annual tribute reached 216,000 jin of compressed tea.

sentences.zh: 建炎以來，葉濃、楊等相因為亂，園丁亡散，遂罷之。

translations.literal: Since Jianyan, Ye Nong, Yang, and others had successive disorder; gardeners fled and scattered, and [the garden] was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jianyan rebellions led by Ye Nong, Yang, and others scattered the gardeners, the imperial garden was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，蠲未起大龍鳳茶一千七百二十八斤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, [they] remitted one thousand seven hundred twenty-eight jin of Great Dragon-Phoenix tea not yet produced.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 2 (1132) the court remitted 1,728 jin of Great Dragon-Phoenix tea not yet tendered.

sentences.zh: 五年，復減大龍鳳及京鋌之半。

translations.literal: In year 5, Great Dragon-Phoenix and capital ingot [tea] were again reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Great Dragon-Phoenix and capital ingot tribute were halved again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，興榷場，遂取臘茶為榷場本，凡胯、截、片、鋌，不以高下多少，官盡榷之，申嚴私販入海之禁。

translations.literal: In year 12, monopoly exchange markets were established; tribute tea was then taken as monopoly-market capital—for all cakes, sections, slices, and ingots, regardless of grade high or low or quantity more or less, the government monopolized them entirely and strictly announced the ban on private sale going to sea.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 monopoly markets opened, tribute tea became their stock-in-trade, and the state monopolized every grade of cake, section, slice, and ingot tea while tightening bans on private export by sea.

sentences.zh: 議者請鬻建茶於臨安，移茶司事於建州買發。

translations.literal: Discussants requested selling Jian tea at Lin'an and shifting tea-office affairs to Jian Prefecture for purchase and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers proposed selling Jian tea at Lin'an and moving procurement to Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，以失陷引錢，復令通商。

translations.literal: The next year, because permit-money receipts were lost and deficient, [they] again ordered general trade permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with permit revenues falling short, free trade was restored.

sentences.zh: 自是上供龍鳳、京鋌茶料，凡製作之費、篚笥之式，令漕司專之。

translations.literal: From this time, for tribute Dragon-Phoenix and capital ingot tea materials, all production costs and bamboo hamper styles were ordered handled exclusively by transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter transport commissioners alone handled production costs and hamper styles for tribute Dragon-Phoenix and capital ingot teas.

sentences.zh: 蜀茶之細者，其品視南方已下，惟廣漢之趙坡，合州之水南，峨眉之白牙，雅安之蒙頂，土人亦珍之，但所產甚微，非江、建比也。

translations.literal: For fine Shu tea, its grades were below the South; only Zhaopo of Guanghan, Shuinan of He Prefecture, Baiya of Emei, and Mengding of Ya'an—local people also treasured them—but what was produced was extremely slight, not comparable to Jiang or Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fine Shu teas ranked below southeastern grades; only Zhaopo in Guanghan, Shuinan in Hezhou, Baiya on Emei, and Mengding in Ya'an were locally prized, yet output was tiny compared with Jiangnan or Jianning.

sentences.zh: 舊無榷禁，熙寧間，始置提舉司，收歲課三十萬；

translations.literal: Formerly there was no monopoly prohibition; in the Xining period, a supervisory office was first established, collecting an annual levy of three hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Tea had once been free of monopoly; in Xining a supervisory office was set up, yielding three hundred thousand strings annually;

sentences.zh: 至元豐中，累增至百萬。

translations.literal: by Yuanfeng it had cumulatively increased to one million.
translations.idiomatic: by Yuanfeng cumulative receipts reached one million.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，成都轉運判官趙開言榷茶、買馬五害，請“用嘉祐故事盡罷榷茶，而令漕司買馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan, Chengdu transport vice-commissioner Zhao Kai spoke of five harms from monopolizing tea and buying horses, requesting "use the Jiayou precedent to abolish tea monopoly entirely and order transport commissioners to buy horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 Chengdu transport vice-commissioner Zhao Kai listed five harms of the tea monopoly and horse trade, asking “to follow the Jiayou precedent by ending tea monopoly and letting transport offices buy horses.

sentences.zh: 或未能然，亦當減額以蘇園戶，輕價以惠行商，如此則私販衰而盜賊息。

translations.literal: Or if that could not be done, still quotas should be reduced to revive plantation households and prices lightened to benefit traveling merchants—thus private trafficking would decline and banditry cease.
translations.idiomatic: Failing that, quotas should be cut to relieve growers and prices lowered for merchants, so smuggling would fall and banditry subside.”

sentences.zh: ”遂以開同主管川、秦茶馬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Kai was made concurrent supervisor of Sichuan and Qin tea and horses.
translations.idiomatic: ” Kai was then appointed to supervise Sichuan and Qin tea and horse affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，開至成都，大更茶法，仿蔡京都茶場法，以引給茶商，即園戶市茶，百斤為一大引，除其十勿算。

translations.literal: In year 2, Kai reached Chengdu and greatly changed the tea law, imitating Cai Jing's capital tea-market law—issuing permits to tea merchants, who then bought tea from plantation households; one hundred jin made one great permit, deducting ten jin not counted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Kai reached Chengdu and overhauled tea law on Cai Jing's capital model: merchants received permits, bought from growers, and took one great permit per hundred jin with ten jin tax-free.

sentences.zh: 置合同場以譏其出入，重私商之禁，為茶市以通交易。

translations.literal: [They] established joint-contract depots to inspect entry and exit, strengthened prohibitions on private merchants, and made tea markets to facilitate exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Joint-contract depots inspected traffic, private trade was strictly banned, and public tea markets were opened for exchange.

sentences.zh: 每斤引錢春七十、夏五十，市利頭子錢不預焉。

translations.literal: Permit money per jin was seventy in spring and fifty in summer; market-profit head money was not included therein.
translations.idiomatic: Permit fees were seventy cash per jin in spring and fifty in summer, excluding market surcharges.

sentences.zh: 所過征一錢，所止一錢五分。

translations.literal: Passing transit levied one cash; stopping levied one cash five.
translations.idiomatic: Transit dues were one cash per jin; stopping dues one and a half.

sentences.zh: 自後引息錢至一百五萬緡。

translations.literal: Afterward permit-interest money reached one million five hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Permit revenues later reached 1.5 million strings.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，都大茶馬韓球盡取園戶加饒之茶為額，茶司歲收二百萬，而買馬之數不加多。

translations.literal: By year 17, Grand Tea-Horse Commissioner Han Qiu took all plantation households' extra-bestowal tea as quota; the tea office yearly collected two million, yet the number of horses bought did not increase.
translations.idiomatic: By year 17 grand commissioner Han Qiu counted growers' bonus tea toward quotas; the tea office took in two million strings yearly while horse purchases barely rose.

sentences.zh: 乾道末年，青羌作亂，茶司增長細馬名色等錢歲三十萬。

translations.literal: At the end of Qiandao, Qing Qiang rebelled; the tea office increased fine-horse name-and-grade and related money by three hundred thousand yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qiandao, after Qing Qiang revolted, the tea office added three hundred thousand strings yearly in fees for fine horses and related charges.

sentences.zh: 淳熙六年以後，累減園戶重額錢十六萬，又減引息錢十六萬。

translations.literal: After the sixth year of Chunxi, plantation households' heavy-quota money was cumulatively reduced by one hundred sixty thousand; permit-interest money was again reduced by one hundred sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Chunxi 6 growers' excess-quota payments were cut by 160,000 strings in all, and permit-interest fees by another 160,000.

sentences.zh: 至紹熙初，楊輔為使，遂定為法。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Shaoxi, Yang Fu as commissioner then fixed it as law.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoxi commissioner Yang Fu codified the revised rates as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 成都府、利州路二十三場，歲產茶二千一百二萬斤，通博馬物帛歲收錢二百四十九萬三千餘緡。

translations.literal: Chengdu Prefecture and Lizhou Circuit had twenty-three markets; yearly tea production was twenty-one million two hundred thousand jin; through barter for horses and goods and silks yearly money collected was two million four hundred ninety-three thousand-odd strings.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three markets in Chengdu and Lizhou produced 21.2 million jin of tea yearly and took in 2,493,000-odd strings from horse barter and related trade.

sentences.zh: 朝廷歲以一百一十三萬緡隸總領所贍軍，然茶馬司率多難之；

translations.literal: The court yearly took one million one hundred thirty thousand strings assigned to the general supervisory office to supply the army, yet the tea-horse office mostly found it difficult;
translations.idiomatic: The court diverted 1,130,000 strings yearly to the general supervisory office for army support, a levy the tea-horse office often resisted;

sentences.zh: 乾道以後，歲撥止一二十萬緡，至淳熙十年，遂以五十萬緡為準。

translations.literal: after Qiandao, yearly allocations were only one hundred twenty thousand strings; by the tenth year of Chunxi, five hundred thousand strings was then taken as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: after Qiandao annual transfers fell to about 120,000 strings, and by Chunxi 10 the quota was fixed at 500,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 宋初，經理蜀茶，置互市於原、渭、德順三郡，以市蕃夷之馬；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, managing Shu tea, [they] established mutual markets in Yuan, Wei, and Deshun—the three commanderies—to trade for Fan and Yi horses;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty Shu tea was organized and mutual markets opened in Yuan, Wei, and Deshun to buy tribal horses;

sentences.zh: 熙寧間，又置場於熙河。

translations.literal: in the Xining period, markets were again established in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: in Xining a market was added at Xihe as well.

sentences.zh: 南渡以來，文、黎、珍、敘、南平、長寧、階、和凡八場，其間盧甘蕃馬歲一至焉，洮州蕃馬或一月或兩月一至焉，疊州蕃馬或半年或三月一至焉，皆良馬也。

translations.literal: Since the southern crossing, Wen, Li, Zhen, Xu, Nanping, Changning, Jie, and He—eight markets in all; among them Lugan Fan horses came once a year, Taozhou Fan horses perhaps once a month or once in two months, Diezhou Fan horses perhaps once in half a year or once in three months—all were fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south eight markets operated—at Wen, Li, Zhen, Xu, Nanping, Changning, Jie, and He—supplying fine horses from Lugan yearly, from Taozhou monthly or bimonthly, and from Diezhou every three to six months.

sentences.zh: 其他諸蕃馬多駑，大率皆以互市為利，宋朝曲示懷遠之恩，亦以是羈縻之。

translations.literal: Other various Fan horses were mostly nags; broadly all took mutual markets as profit—the Song court bent to display favor-granting distant kindness, also thereby keeping them on loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: Most other tribal horses were poor nags; tribes profited chiefly from trade, and the Song court cultivated favor and loose-rein control through these markets.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十四年，復黎州及雅州碉門靈犀砦易馬場。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Shaoxing, Lizhou and Yazhou Diaomen Lingxi Stockade horse-exchange markets were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 24 (1154) horse markets were restored at Lizhou and at Diaomen Lingxi stockade in Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，川、秦八場馬額九千餘匹，淳熙以來，為額萬二千九百九十四匹，自後所市未嚐及焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiandao, the eight markets of Chuan and Qin had a horse quota of more than nine thousand head; since Chunxi the quota was set at twelve thousand nine hundred ninety-four head—afterward what was purchased never reached it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiandao the eight Sichuan and Qin markets were allotted more than nine thousand horses; since Chunxi the quota rose to 12,994, yet purchases never met even that figure.
